example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: Cái áo khoác nhìn như phim cổ điển!
l1.ex: Cái áo khoác này it's giving ngôi sao phim xưa.

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: Hôm nay tệ, nhưng mai tới rồi!
l1.ex: Chin up, mai sẽ tốt hơn thôi.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: Cơm xong rồi. Ai đói nào?
l1.ex: Cơm xong rồi nè, dig in đi!

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: Phải đi rồi. Vô học rồi!
l1.ex: Catch you later, tui phải đi rồi!

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: Bàn thắng giây chót. Tụi mình thắng!
l1.ex: Tụi tui ghi bàn giây chót. Epic win!

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

l1.hook: Nói thiệt phim đó sao?
l1.ex: Ngl, tui mê phim đó lắm.

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: Bánh của tui xẹp. Ai cũng thấy!
l1.ex: Bánh tui xẹp lép. Epic fail thiệt sự!

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

l1.hook: Mua quà cho cổ? Ai chung không?
l1.ex: Mọi người chip in mua quà cho cổ nha.

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: Mai thi rồi. Bắt đầu từ đâu đây?
l1.ex: Vậy game plan là gì đây?

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

l1.hook: Nhìn đôi giày mới của tui đi!
l1.ex: Đôi giày đó fire thiệt!

facts.def: A casual way to ask someone to repeat.

example.text: Come again? It's too loud here.

misuse.text: Don't say 'come again' when you heard clearly.

l1.hook: Xin lỗi, nhạc to quá!
l1.ex: Come again? Ở đây ồn quá.

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

l1.hook: Tuần sau thi cuối kỳ. Hoảng rồi!
l1.ex: Tối nay tui phải hit the books.

facts.def: People who love the same show or band.

example.text: The fandom loves this band.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers a 'fandom'.
misuse.why: It means devoted fans of one thing.

l1.hook: Ai mê ban nhạc này nhất?
l1.ex: Fandom rất mê ban nhạc này.

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

l1.hook: Chuyến leo núi đó dài vô tận!
l1.ex: Leo núi xong tui dog tired luôn.

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: Nhìn ra ngoài đi! Lấy dù nhanh!
l1.ex: Trời đang raining cats and dogs luôn!

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

l1.hook: Báo nhanh: sếp tới kìa!
l1.ex: Heads up nha, buổi họp bắt đầu sớm đó.

facts.def: Used to say you agree to a plan or want to do it.

example.text: We're going bowling tonight. Are you down?

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm down' when you feel sad.
misuse.why: It can also mean feeling low.

l1.hook: Tối nay đi bowling, ai đi nào?
l1.ex: Tối nay đi bowling nè. Bạn có down không?

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: أفضل بيتزا في المدينة. صدقني؟ "no cap"
l1.ex: هذه البيتزا هي الأفضل في المدينة، 'no cap'.

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: لقد خسر ثم استاء! "salty"
l1.ex: إنه 'salty' لأنني فزت في لعبة الورق.

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: القطة قفزت في الصندوق! "I'm dead"
l1.ex: القطة قفزت في الصندوق. 'I'm dead'!

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.hook: البيتزا بأكملها اختفت! "pig out"
l1.ex: لقد قمنا بـ 'pig out' على البيتزا ليلة أمس.

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: بيتزا في السادسة، اتفقنا؟ "bet"
l1.ex: بيتزا في السادسة؟ 'bet'.

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: بيتزا وفيلم مجدداً؟ "basic"
l1.ex: خطتي لنهاية الأسبوع "basic": بيتزا وفيلم.

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: توقف هذان الاثنان عن الكلام. لماذا؟ "beef"
l1.ex: بينهما "beef" بسبب لعبة.

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: غرفتك تبدو مثل بينتريست! "aesthetic"
l1.ex: مكتبك يبدو "aesthetic" جدًا.

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.hook: رأى أبي الغرفة الفوضوية! "blow a fuse"
l1.ex: انفجر (blow a fuse) بسبب الغرفة الفوضوية.

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: معكرونة أمي بطعم "bussin" الليلة!
l1.ex: معكرونة أمي "bussin" الليلة.

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: شكراً جزيلاً على التوصيلة!
l1.ex: شكراً على التوصيلة! "Anytime".

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: خمس دقائق، ثم أعود!
l1.ex: سأعود قريباً، سأكون "AFK" لمدة خمس دقائق.

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: أين ذهب المفتاح؟
l1.ex: أين المفتاح؟ "Beats me".

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: فشلت الخطة. ماذا الآن؟
l1.ex: فشلت الخطة. "Back to square one".

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: انظر إلى سعر هذا المعطف!
l1.ex: هذا المعطف يكلف "an arm and a leg".

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: أوه، "by the way" شيء آخر!
l1.ex: "by the way"، تبدأ الحفلة في الساعة السابعة.

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: هل حصلت لنا على تذاكر مجانية؟
l1.ex: هل حصلت لنا على تذاكر مجانية؟ هذا "awesome"!

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: قطة نعسانة. شعوري بالضبط!
l1.ex: تلك القطة النعسانة تمثل "big mood".

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.hook: يوم الاختبار. كيف كان أداؤك؟
l1.ex: لقد "aced" اختبار التاريخ اليوم!

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: عطلة نهاية أسبوع ممطرة. موسم كامل. هيا!
l1.ex: سأقوم بـ "binge-watch" لهذا المسلسل طوال عطلة نهاية الأسبوع.

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: عمل كثير جداً. أنا "burned out"!
l1.ex: بعد الامتحانات، شعرت بأني "burned out" تماماً.

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: الأسبوع الماضي كنت مريضاً، واليوم أنا "back on my feet"!
l1.ex: أنا أخيراً "back on my feet".

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: أحتاجه "ASAP"!
l1.ex: من فضلك أرسل لي الملاحظات "ASAP".

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: فيلم الليلة في السادسة، "cool"؟
l1.ex: "Cool"، أراك في السادسة!

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: هو لا يدفع ثمن الغداء أبداً، إنه "cheap"!
l1.ex: إنه "cheap" جداً لدرجة أنه لا يشتري الغداء.

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.hook: هي "call out" خطأي أمام الجميع!
l1.ex: لقد "called me out" بسبب تأخري.

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.hook: يوم المقابلة. "dressed to impress" بدلة وربطة عنق!
l1.ex: إنه "dressed to impress" من أجل المقابلة.

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.hook: ساعتان من الشرائح نفسها، "bored stiff"
l1.ex: كنت "bored stiff" في تلك الحصة.

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.hook: السبت. "cheat day"؟ نظام غذائي؟ أي نظام غذائي؟
l1.ex: يوم السبت هو الـ "cheat day" الخاص بي.

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.hook: من يعرف كل أسرارك؟ "bestie"
l1.ex: أنا والـ "bestie" نحب التاكو.

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.hook: نجحت في الاختبار؟ "big w"!
l1.ex: هل اجتزت الاختبار؟ هذا "big W"!

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.hook: بيتزا بالأناناس هي الأفضل! "hot take"
l1.ex: إليك الـ "hot take" الخاص بي: الأناناس مكانه على البيتزا.

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: تعثر في مسرحية المدرسة! "blooper"
l1.ex: هذا الـ "blooper" جعل الصف بأكمله يضحك.

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.hook: كم سيكلف ذلك؟ اعطني "ballpark figure".
l1.ex: أعطني "ballpark figure".

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.hook: ليلة ألعاب في منزلي! "count me in".
l1.ex: ليلة الألعاب؟ "count me in"!

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.hook: شغّل هذه الأغنية بصوت أعلى! إنها "banger".
l1.ex: هذه الأغنية الجديدة "banger"!

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

l1.hook: جوارب مع صندل؟ حقًا؟ "big yikes".
l1.ex: جوارب مع صندل؟ "Big yikes".

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

l1.hook: أضواء المسرح مضاءة. قد حدث لي "blank out" وعقلي فارغ!
l1.ex: لقد "blanked out" في منتصف خطابي.

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

l1.hook: ثلاث ساعات من الفيديوهات السخيفة! "brain rot".
l1.ex: كثرة الفيديوهات تسبب لي "brain rot".

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

l1.hook: ليس لدي وقت فراغ هذا الأسبوع! أنا "busy as a bee".
l1.ex: أنا "busy as a bee" هذا الأسبوع.

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

l1.hook: إنه بارد جدًا في الخارج. هل أنت مستعد؟ "bundle up"
l1.ex: "Bundle up"، الجو بارد جدًا في الخارج!

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

l1.hook: ليس هناك وقت الآن. لاحقًا؟ "circle back"
l1.ex: دعنا "circle back" إلى ذلك بعد الغداء.

facts.def: Used to accept someone's point.

example.text: Fair enough, let's try your idea.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fair enough' to a rude insult.
misuse.why: It sounds like you agree with them.

l1.hook: انتظر، استمع إلى مبرراتي أولًا! "fair enough"
l1.ex: "Fair enough"، لنجرّب فكرتك.

facts.def: Describes things that are corny or too sweet.

example.text: That movie was so cheesy.

misuse.text: Don't call her poem 'cheesy' at the party.
misuse.why: It sounds mean about heartfelt effort.

l1.hook: رسالة حبه كانت على قافية. يا إلهي! "cheesy"
l1.ex: ذلك الفيلم كان "cheesy".

facts.def: To answer criticism quickly and cleverly.

example.text: She clapped back with a great reply.

misuse.text: Don't 'clap back' at a parent's advice.

l1.hook: لقد سخر منها، لكنها قامت بـ "clap back" قاسي!
l1.ex: هي "clap back" بردة حادة.

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

l1.hook: سترة جديدة، أحذية جديدة، ثقة جديدة! "drip"
l1.ex: سترة جميلة، لديك "drip" اليوم.

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: تم إلغاء الرحلة. الجميع حزين! "bummed out"
l1.ex: أنا "bummed out" بشأن الرحلة.

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

l1.hook: تذوق هذا وأخبرني! "chef's kiss"
l1.ex: كانت الشربة "chef's kiss".

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

l1.hook: شكرًا لإنقاذك واجبي! "bro"
l1.ex: شكرًا، "bro"، أنقذتني!

facts.def: To lead a team to victory with great skill.

example.text: Mia carried us in the final round.

misuse.text: Don't say 'she carried us' about a lazy teammate.
misuse.why: It praises someone who did the work.

l1.hook: فازت بالمباراة بمفردها! "carry"
l1.ex: لقد قامت ميا بـ "carry" الفريق في الجولة الأخيرة.

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

l1.hook: أكلت كعكتك!
l1.ex: أكلت كعكتك. "just kidding"

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

l1.hook: نسيت ملاحظاتي. أوه!
l1.ex: نسيت ملاحظاتي. أنا "cooked".

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

l1.hook: هي لا تشرب إلا شايًا فخمًا!
l1.ex: هذا المقهى "bougie" جدًا.

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

l1.hook: هل تريد الذهاب إلى العرض المتأخر؟
l1.ex: أنا متعب، لذا "count me out".

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: شكر الجميع، حتى الخصوم!
l1.ex: مدربنا "class act" حقيقي.

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: نسيت واجبك المنزلي مجدداً؟ "bruh"!
l1.ex: "Bruh"، هل نسيت واجبك المنزلي مجدداً؟

facts.def: To keep working late into the night.

example.text: We burned the midnight oil last night.

misuse.text: Don't say it about lighting candles.

l1.hook: ما زلت تعمل حتى الثانية صباحاً؟ هل تقوم بـ "burn the midnight oil"؟
l1.ex: لقد قمنا بـ "burn the midnight oil" الليلة الماضية.

facts.mean: A title that tricks you to click.
facts.def: A catchy headline that isn't worth reading.

example.text: That title is pure clickbait.

misuse.text: Don't call a real news story 'clickbait'.

l1.hook: "لن تصدق ما حدث!" حقاً؟ مجرد "clickbait"!
l1.ex: هذا العنوان هو "clickbait" خالص.

facts.def: To decide to finish work or an activity for now.

example.text: We're tired, let's call it a day.

misuse.text: Don't 'call it a day' before the deadline.

l1.hook: نحن متعبون. ماذا الآن؟ "call it a day"
l1.ex: لقد تعبنا، لنقم بـ "call it a day".

facts.def: To begin to feel ill with something like a cold.

example.text: I think I'm coming down with a cold.

misuse.text: Don't say you 'came down with' a gift.
misuse.why: It means starting to get sick.

l1.hook: حلقي يؤلمني. أووه! يبدو أنني على وشك أن "come down with" مرضا ما!
l1.ex: أعتقد أنني بدأت "come down with" زكام.

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

l1.hook: FYI: مجرد خبر بسيط!
l1.ex: "FYI"، المحل يغلق في الخامسة.

facts.def: Used to say you accept an idea.

example.text: Pizza or tacos? Fine by me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fine by me' when you're upset.
misuse.why: People will think you truly don't mind.

l1.hook: بيتزا أم تاكو، اختر أنت، الأمر "fine by me".
l1.ex: بيتزا أم تاكو؟ "fine by me".

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

l1.hook: دعابة أبي التافهة مجدداً. هل هي "corny" حقاً؟
l1.ex: مزاح أبي "corny" جداً.

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.hook: انفجرت محادثة المجموعة على لا شيء! الكثير من الـ "drama".
l1.ex: لا أريد أي "drama" هذا العام.

facts.def: A moment to show your outfit and get opinions.

example.text: Quick fit check before school!

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'fit check' at the gym.

l1.hook: الملابس جاهزة. ما رأيكم قبل المدرسة؟
l1.ex: "fit check" سريع قبل المدرسة!

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.hook: تبدو حزينة. ماذا الآن؟ كيف نجعلها "cheer up"؟
l1.ex: "Cheer up"، نحن نتناول البيتزا!

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.hook: يوم حزين؟ حساء دافئ!
l1.ex: الحساء الدافئ هو الـ "comfort food" بالنسبة لي.

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: من يدرس معك كل ليلة؟
l1.ex: إنه الـ "buddy" الخاص بي في الدراسة.

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.hook: هدف في الثانية الأخيرة يحسم الفوز!
l1.ex: هدف الدقيقة الأخيرة كان "clutch" بحق.

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: هل هذا المتجر حقيقي؟
l1.ex: هذا المتجر "legit"، أختي اشترت أحذية من هناك.

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

l1.hook: أنا جديد هنا. يرجى الترفق بي و"cut me some slack"!
l1.ex: تساهل معي ("Cut me some slack")، فأنا ما زلت جديداً.

facts.def: To cost so much that you can't afford it.

example.text: Don't worry, this lunch won't break the bank.

misuse.text: Don't say 'break the bank' at a bank.
misuse.why: It only means costing too much.

l1.hook: هل الغداء مكلف للغاية بحيث ينطبق عليه عبارة "break the bank"؟
l1.ex: لا تقلق، وجبة الغداء هذه لن تكلف ثروة ("break the bank").

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: تعال في أي وقت هذا الأسبوع! يمكنك استخدام "drop by".
l1.ex: لا تتردد في أن تمر علينا ("drop by") في أي وقت.

facts.def: Used when someone is doing really well at something.

example.text: You're crushing it at your new job!

misuse.text: Don't tell a struggling friend 'crushing it' sarcastically.

l1.hook: الأسبوع الأول وأنت بالفعل الأفضل مبيعاً! أنت بحق "crushing it"!
l1.ex: أنت تبدع حقاً ("crushing it") في عملك الجديد!

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: تم إلغاء الرحلة. يا للإحباط! إنه أمر "bummer".
l1.ex: هل أُلغيت الرحلة؟ يا له من أمر "bummer".

facts.def: To study many things quickly just before a test.

example.text: I must cram for math.

misuse.text: Don't 'cram' for a three-year course.
misuse.why: Cramming only works for short tests.

l1.hook: الامتحان غداً. لم أدرس بعد!
l1.ex: يجب أن أقوم بـ "cram" لمادة الرياضيات.

facts.mean: Scroll bad news for too long.
facts.def: To keep reading sad online news without stopping.

example.text: Stop doomscrolling and go to sleep.

misuse.text: Don't say 'doomscroll' about reading a recipe.

l1.hook: منتصف الليل. وما زلت أتصفح الأخبار السيئة!
l1.ex: توقف عن الـ "doomscrolling" واذهب للنوم.

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: الوقت متأخر وأنا نعسان!
l1.ex: سأذهب لـ "catch some Zs".

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

l1.hook: قيلولة واحدة، وأصبحت أفضل!
l1.ex: بعد القيلولة، أشعر أنني "good as new".

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

l1.hook: يبدأ الاجتماع. من يبدأ أولاً؟
l1.ex: فلنقم بـ "get the ball rolling" بطرح الأفكار.

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

l1.hook: هل يمكنني الاعتماد عليك؟
l1.ex: بيتزا الليلة؟ "For sure"!

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

l1.hook: انتهت الحفلة في الثامنة. أحقاً؟
l1.ex: تلك الحفلة كانت نوعاً ما "lame".

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

l1.hook: نبتسم، لكننا نتنافس!
l1.ex: إنها "frenemy" بالنسبة لي، وتتنافس معي دائماً.

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: ذاك المعطف يبدو وكأنه من الأفلام القديمة!
l1.ex: هذا المعطف "it's giving" طابع نجم سينمائي قديم.

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: يوم صعب، لكن الغد قادم!
l1.ex: "Chin up"، غداً سيكون أفضل.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: العشاء جاهز. من جائع؟
l1.ex: العشاء جاهز، لذا "dig in"!

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: يجب أن أذهب، الدرس يبدأ الآن! "catch you later"!
l1.ex: "Catch you later"، يجب أن أذهب!

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: هدف في الثواني الأخيرة، لقد فزنا! هذا هو الـ "epic win" الحقيقي!
l1.ex: سجلنا في الثانية الأخيرة. "Epic win"!

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

l1.hook: ما رأيك الصادق حول ذلك الفيلم؟
l1.ex: "Ngl"، لقد أحببت ذلك الفيلم.

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: لقد انهارت كعكتي، وشاهدني الجميع! هذا "epic fail".
l1.ex: هبطت كعكتي تماماً. "Epic fail" تام!

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

l1.hook: هدية لها؟ أي أحد يريد أن "chip in"؟
l1.ex: فلنقم جميعًا بـ "chip in" لشراء هديتها.

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: الامتحان غدًا. ما هي الـ "game plan" لدينا؟
l1.ex: إذن، ما هي الـ "game plan"؟

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

l1.hook: انظر إلى حذائي الرياضي الجديد! إنه "fire"!
l1.ex: هذا الحذاء الرياضي "fire" حقاً!

facts.def: A casual way to ask someone to repeat.

example.text: Come again? It's too loud here.

misuse.text: Don't say 'come again' when you heard clearly.

l1.hook: عذراً، الموسيقى صاخبة جداً! هل يمكنك أن "come again"؟
l1.ex: "come again"؟ المكان صاخب جدًا هنا.

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

l1.hook: الامتحانات النهائية الأسبوع القادم. حان وقت الـ "hit the books"!
l1.ex: يجب عليّ أن "hit the books" الليلة.

facts.def: People who love the same show or band.

example.text: The fandom loves this band.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers a 'fandom'.
misuse.why: It means devoted fans of one thing.

l1.hook: من يحب هذه الفرقة أكثر؟ هذا هو الـ "fandom".
l1.ex: يحب الـ "fandom" هذه الفرقة.

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

l1.hook: كانت تلك النزهة تبدو بلا نهاية!
l1.ex: أنا "dog tired" بعد تلك النزهة السيرية الطويلة.

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: انظر إلى الخارج! خذ مظلة!
l1.ex: إنها "raining cats and dogs"!

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

l1.hook: تحذير سريع: المدير قادم!
l1.ex: مجرد "heads up"، الاجتماع سيبدأ مبكراً.

facts.def: Used to say you agree to a plan or want to do it.

example.text: We're going bowling tonight. Are you down?

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm down' when you feel sad.
misuse.why: It can also mean feeling low.

l1.hook: البولينج الليلة، من سيأتي؟
l1.ex: نحن ذاهبون للبولينغ الليلة. هل أنت "I'm down"؟

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: Beste Pizza in der Stadt. Glaub mir, no cap.
l1.ex: Diese Pizza ist die beste der Stadt, „no cap“.

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: Er hat verloren, dann war er salty.
l1.ex: Er ist „salty“, weil ich das Kartenspiel gewonnen habe.

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: Die Katze sprang in die Kiste! I'm dead.
l1.ex: Die Katze ist in den Karton gesprungen. „I'm dead“!

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.hook: Die ganze Pizza ist weg! "pig out"
l1.ex: Wir haben gestern Abend bei Pizza „pigged out“.

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: Pizza um sechs, bet?
l1.ex: Pizza um sechs? „Bet“.

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: Schon wieder Pizza und ein Film?
l1.ex: Mein Wochenendplan ist „basic“: Pizza und ein Film.

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: Die zwei reden nicht mehr miteinander. Warum?
l1.ex: Sie haben „beef“ wegen eines Spiels.

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: Dein Zimmer sieht aus wie auf Pinterest!
l1.ex: Dein Schreibtisch sieht so „aesthetic“ aus.

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.hook: Papa hat das unordentliche Zimmer gesehen!
l1.ex: Er ist wegen des chaotischen Zimmers ausgerastet. "blow a fuse"

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: Mamas Pasta schmeckt heute Abend unglaublich!
l1.ex: Mamas Pasta ist heute Abend „bussin“.

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: Danke für die Mitfahrgelegenheit! anytime.
l1.ex: Danke fürs Mitnehmen! „Anytime“.

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: Fünf Minuten, dann bin ich zurück! afk.
l1.ex: Gleich zurück, ich bin für fünf Minuten AFK.

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: Wo ist der Schlüssel hin? beats me.
l1.ex: Wo ist der Schlüssel? „Beats me“.

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: Plan gescheitert. Jetzt was? back to square one.
l1.ex: Plan gescheitert. „Back to square one“.

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: Sieh dir den Preis dieses Mantels an – er kostet 'arm and a leg'.
l1.ex: Dieser Mantel kostet „an arm and a leg“.

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: Oh, „by the way“, noch etwas!
l1.ex: 'By the way', die Party fängt um sieben an.

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: Du hast uns kostenlose Tickets? Das ist „awesome“.
l1.ex: Du hast uns Freikarten besorgt? Das ist 'awesome'!

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: Schläfriger Kater. Genau mein „big mood“.
l1.ex: Diese müde Katze ist ein 'big mood'.

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.hook: Prüfungstag. Wie lief es bei dir?
l1.ex: Ich habe heute meinen Geschichtstest 'aced'!

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: Regnerisches Wochenende. Ganze Staffel. Los, "binge-watch"!
l1.ex: Ich werde diese Serie das ganze Wochenende 'binge-watchen'.

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: Zu viel Arbeit. Ich bin 'burned out'!
l1.ex: Nach den Prüfungen fühlte ich mich total 'burned out'.

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: Letzte Woche krank, heute wieder 'back on my feet'!
l1.ex: Ich bin endlich wieder 'back on my feet'.

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: Ich brauche es 'ASAP'!
l1.ex: Bitte schick mir die Notizen 'ASAP'.

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: Film heute Abend um sechs, 'cool'?
l1.ex: 'Cool', wir sehen uns um sechs!

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: Er bezahlt nie fürs Mittagessen, so 'cheap'!
l1.ex: Er ist zu 'cheap', um sich ein Mittagessen zu kaufen.

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.hook: Sie hat allen meinen Fehler gezeigt! "call out"
l1.ex: Sie hat mich dafür kritisiert („called me out“), dass ich zu spät war.

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.hook: Interview‑Tag. Anzug und Krawatte – „dressed to impress“.
l1.ex: Er ist für das Vorstellungsgespräch „dressed to impress“ gekleidet.

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.hook: Zwei Stunden dieselben Folien – ich bin „bored stiff“.
l1.ex: Ich war in diesem Kurs „bored stiff“.

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.hook: Samstag. Diät? Welche Diät? – „cheat day“.
l1.ex: Samstag ist mein „cheat day“.

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.hook: Wer kennt all deine Geheimnisse? Das ist deine „bestie“.
l1.ex: Meine bestie und ich lieben Tacos.

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.hook: Du hast den Test bestanden? "big W"!
l1.ex: Du hast den Test bestanden? "Big W"!

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.hook: Ananaspizza ist das Beste! "hot take"
l1.ex: Hier ist mein "hot take": Ananas gehört auf Pizza.

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: Er ist in der Schulaufführung gestolpert! "blooper"
l1.ex: Dieser "blooper" brachte die ganze Klasse zum Lachen.

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.hook: Wie viel wird es kosten? "ballpark figure"
l1.ex: Gib mir eine "ballpark figure".

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.hook: Spieleabend bei mir! "count me in"
l1.ex: Spieleabend? "count me in"!

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.hook: Spiel das Lied lauter!
l1.ex: Dieser neue Song ist ein "banger"!

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

l1.hook: Socken mit Sandalen? Wirklich?
l1.ex: Socken mit Sandalen? "Big yikes".

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

l1.hook: Bühnenlichter an. Mein Kopf ist leer!
l1.ex: Ich habe mitten in meiner Rede „blanked out“.

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

l1.hook: Drei Stunden alberner Videos!
l1.ex: Zu viele Videos geben mir "brain rot".

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

l1.hook: Keine Freizeit diese Woche!
l1.ex: Ich bin diese Woche "busy as a bee".

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

l1.hook: Es ist eiskalt draußen. Bereit? "bundle up"
l1.ex: 'Bundle up', es ist eiskalt draußen!

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

l1.hook: Jetzt keine Zeit. Können wir später "circle back"?
l1.ex: Lass uns nach dem Mittagessen darauf zurückkommen ("circle back").

facts.def: Used to accept someone's point.

example.text: Fair enough, let's try your idea.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fair enough' to a rude insult.
misuse.why: It sounds like you agree with them.

l1.hook: Warte, hör dir zuerst meine Begründung an!
l1.ex: Fair enough, lass uns deine Idee ausprobieren.

facts.def: Describes things that are corny or too sweet.

example.text: That movie was so cheesy.

misuse.text: Don't call her poem 'cheesy' at the party.
misuse.why: It sounds mean about heartfelt effort.

l1.hook: Seine Liebesnotiz reimte sich. Pfui!
l1.ex: Der Film war so cheesy.

facts.def: To answer criticism quickly and cleverly.

example.text: She clapped back with a great reply.

misuse.text: Don't 'clap back' at a parent's advice.

l1.hook: Er hat sie verspottet. Sie hat geantwortet!
l1.ex: Sie hat mit einer großartigen Antwort clapped back.

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

l1.hook: Neue Jacke, neue Schuhe, neues Selbstbewusstsein!
l1.ex: Schicke Jacke, du hast heute "drip".

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: Reise abgesagt. Alle sind traurig!
l1.ex: Ich bin "bummed out" wegen der Reise.

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

l1.hook: Probier das und sag mir, ob es ein "chef's kiss" ist.
l1.ex: Die Suppe war "chef's kiss".

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

l1.hook: Danke, dass du meine Hausaufgaben gerettet hast, bro!
l1.ex: Danke, bro, du hast mich gerettet!

facts.def: To lead a team to victory with great skill.

example.text: Mia carried us in the final round.

misuse.text: Don't say 'she carried us' about a lazy teammate.
misuse.why: It praises someone who did the work.

l1.hook: Sie hat das Spiel allein gewonnen – ein echtes „carry“.
l1.ex: Mia hat uns in der letzten Runde zum Sieg getragen. "carry"

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

l1.hook: Ich habe deinen Kuchen gegessen, „just kidding“!
l1.ex: Ich habe deinen Kuchen gegessen! "just kidding".

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

l1.hook: Ich habe meine Notizen vergessen. Uh-oh! Das ist „cooked“.
l1.ex: Ich habe meine Notizen vergessen. Ich bin "cooked".

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

l1.hook: Sie trinkt nur edlen Tee – das ist echt „bougie“.
l1.ex: Dieses Café ist so "bougie".

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

l1.hook: Willst du zur Spätshow gehen? „count me out“.
l1.ex: Ich bin müde, also "count me out".

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: Er dankte allen, sogar den Rivalen – ein echtes „class act“.
l1.ex: Unser Trainer ist ein echter "class act".

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: Du hast deine Hausaufgaben schon wieder vergessen, "bruh"?
l1.ex: "Bruh", du hast deine Hausaufgaben schon wieder vergessen?

facts.def: To keep working late into the night.

example.text: We burned the midnight oil last night.

misuse.text: Don't say it about lighting candles.

l1.m: bis spät in die Nacht arbeiten
l1.hook: Noch um zwei Uhr morgens am Arbeiten? ("burn the midnight oil")
l1.ex: Wir haben letzte Nacht „burned the midnight oil“.

facts.mean: A title that tricks you to click.
facts.def: A catchy headline that isn't worth reading.

example.text: That title is pure clickbait.

misuse.text: Don't call a real news story 'clickbait'.

l1.hook: „You won't believe it!“ Wirklich? ("clickbait")
l1.ex: Dieser Titel ist reines "clickbait".

facts.def: To decide to finish work or an activity for now.

example.text: We're tired, let's call it a day.

misuse.text: Don't 'call it a day' before the deadline.

l1.hook: Wir sind müde. Was jetzt? ("call it a day")
l1.ex: Wir sind müde, lass uns "call it a day" sagen.

facts.def: To begin to feel ill with something like a cold.

example.text: I think I'm coming down with a cold.

misuse.text: Don't say you 'came down with' a gift.
misuse.why: It means starting to get sick.

l1.hook: Mein Hals tut weh. Uh‑oh! ("come down with")
l1.ex: Ich glaube, ich bekomme eine Erkältung. ("come down with")

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

l1.hook: Nur ein bisschen Neuigkeiten! ("FYI")
l1.ex: "FYI", das Geschäft schließt um fünf Uhr.

facts.def: Used to say you accept an idea.

example.text: Pizza or tacos? Fine by me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fine by me' when you're upset.
misuse.why: People will think you truly don't mind.

l1.hook: Pizza oder Tacos, du entscheidest. ("fine by me")
l1.ex: Pizza oder Tacos? "Fine by me".

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

l1.hook: Dad's Wortspiel wieder. Ernsthaft? ("corny")
l1.ex: Vaters Witze sind so "corny".

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.hook: Der Gruppenchat ist wegen Nichts explodiert, "drama"!
l1.ex: Ich will dieses Jahr kein "Drama".

facts.def: A moment to show your outfit and get opinions.

example.text: Quick fit check before school!

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'fit check' at the gym.

l1.hook: Outfit fertig. Was sagst du, "fit check"?
l1.ex: Schneller "fit check" vor der Schule!

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.hook: Sie sieht traurig aus. Was jetzt? "Cheer up"!
l1.ex: "Cheer up", wir essen Pizza!

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.hook: Trauriger Tag? Eine warme Suppe ist dein 'comfort food'!
l1.ex: Warme Suppe ist mein "comfort food".

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: Wer ist dein nächtlicher Lern-'buddy'?
l1.ex: Er ist mein Lern-buddy.

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.hook: Ein Tor in letzter Sekunde entscheidet – das ist "clutch"!
l1.ex: Dieses Tor in letzter Minute war so "clutch".

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: Ist dieser Laden 'legit'?
l1.ex: Dieser Laden ist "legit", meine Schwester hat dort Schuhe gekauft.

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

l1.hook: Ich bin neu. Bitte sei nachsichtig, "cut me some slack".
l1.ex: "Cut me some slack", ich bin neu.

facts.def: To cost so much that you can't afford it.

example.text: Don't worry, this lunch won't break the bank.

misuse.text: Don't say 'break the bank' at a bank.
misuse.why: It only means costing too much.

l1.hook: Ist das Mittagessen zu teuer?
l1.ex: Keine Sorge, dieses Mittagessen wird nicht "break the bank".

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: Komm diese Woche jederzeit vorbei, also 'drop by'!
l1.ex: Fühl dich frei, jederzeit "drop by" zu kommen.

facts.def: Used when someone is doing really well at something.

example.text: You're crushing it at your new job!

misuse.text: Don't tell a struggling friend 'crushing it' sarcastically.

l1.hook: Erste Woche und schon Top-Verkäufer – du bist 'crushing it'!
l1.ex: Du bist "crushing it" in deinem neuen Job!

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: Die Reise wurde abgesagt. Ugh, das ist ein 'bummer'!
l1.ex: Die Reise ist abgesagt? Was für ein "bummer".

facts.def: To study many things quickly just before a test.

example.text: I must cram for math.

misuse.text: Don't 'cram' for a three-year course.
misuse.why: Cramming only works for short tests.

l1.hook: Morgen Prüfung, ich habe nicht gelernt – ich muss 'cram'!
l1.ex: Ich muss für Mathe "cram".

facts.mean: Scroll bad news for too long.
facts.def: To keep reading sad online news without stopping.

example.text: Stop doomscrolling and go to sleep.

misuse.text: Don't say 'doomscroll' about reading a recipe.

l1.hook: Mitternacht, ich scroll immer noch schlechte Nachrichten – ich 'doomscroll'!
l1.ex: Hör auf zu 'doomscrollen' und geh schlafen.

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: Es ist spät und ich bin müde, also sollte ich "catch some Zs".
l1.ex: Ich werde "catch some Zs".

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

l1.hook: Ein Nickerchen, und ich bin wieder "good as new".
l1.ex: Nach einem Nickerchen fühle ich mich "good as new".

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

l1.hook: Das Meeting beginnt. Wer soll "get the ball rolling"?
l1.ex: Lass uns "get the ball rolling" mit Ideen.

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

l1.hook: Kann ich mich auf dich verlassen? "for sure".
l1.ex: Pizza heute Abend? "for sure"!

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

l1.hook: Die Party endete um acht. Ernsthaft? "lame".
l1.ex: Die Party war irgendwie "lame".

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

l1.hook: Wir lächeln, aber wir sind 'frenemy'!
l1.ex: Sie ist meine "frenemy", immer im Wettbewerb mit mir.

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: Dieser Mantel sieht aus wie alte Filme!
l1.ex: Dieser Mantel vermittelt den Look eines alten Filmstars. "it's giving"

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: Schwieriger Tag, aber morgen kommt – 'chin up'!
l1.ex: "Chin up", morgen wird es besser.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: Das Abendessen ist fertig. Wer hat Hunger? 'dig in'!
l1.ex: Das Abendessen ist fertig, also "dig in"!

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: Muss los, der Unterricht beginnt jetzt! 'catch you later'!
l1.ex: "Catch you later", ich muss gehen!

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: Tor in der letzten Sekunde. Wir gewinnen! "epic win"
l1.ex: Wir haben in der letzten Sekunde ein Tor geschossen. "epic win"!

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

l1.hook: Ehrliche Meinung zu dem Film? "ngl"
l1.ex: "ngl", ich habe den Film geliebt.

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: Mein Kuchen ist zusammengefallen. Alle haben zugesehen! "epic fail"
l1.ex: Mein Kuchen ist flach geworden. Total "epic fail"!

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

l1.hook: Geschenk für sie? Wer will etwas beisteuern? "chip in"
l1.ex: Lasst uns alle „chip in“ für ihr Geschenk.

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: Test morgen. Wo fangen wir an? "game plan"
l1.ex: Also, was ist unser "game plan"?

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

l1.hook: Schau dir meine neuen Sneaker an! 'fire'!
l1.ex: Die Sneaker sind "fire"!

facts.def: A casual way to ask someone to repeat.

example.text: Come again? It's too loud here.

misuse.text: Don't say 'come again' when you heard clearly.

l1.hook: Entschuldigung, die Musik ist zu laut! 'come again'!
l1.ex: "Come again"? Es ist hier zu laut.

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

l1.hook: Prüfungen nächste Woche. Panikzeit! 'hit the books'!
l1.ex: Ich muss heute Abend "hit the books".

facts.def: People who love the same show or band.

example.text: The fandom loves this band.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers a 'fandom'.
misuse.why: It means devoted fans of one thing.

l1.hook: Wer liebt diese Band am meisten? "fandom"
l1.ex: Das "fandom" liebt diese Band.

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

l1.hook: Die Wanderung fühlte sich endlos an! "dog tired"
l1.ex: Ich bin "dog tired" nach dem langen Aufstieg.

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: Schau nach draußen! Schnapp dir einen Regenschirm, es regnet "raining cats and dogs"!
l1.ex: Es regnet "raining cats and dogs"!

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

l1.hook: Kurze Warnung, "heads up": Der Chef kommt!
l1.ex: Nur ein "heads up": Das Meeting beginnt früh.

facts.def: Used to say you agree to a plan or want to do it.

example.text: We're going bowling tonight. Are you down?

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm down' when you feel sad.
misuse.why: It can also mean feeling low.

l1.hook: Bowling heute Abend, wer kommt? („I'm down“ = ich bin dabei)
l1.ex: Wir gehen heute Abend bowlen. Bist du dabei? „I'm down“.

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: La mejor pizza de la ciudad. Créeme, "no cap".
l1.ex: Esta pizza es la mejor de la ciudad, "no cap".

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: Perdió y luego se puso "salty".
l1.ex: Está "salty" porque gané al juego de cartas.

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: ¡El gato se metió en la caja! "I'm dead".
l1.ex: El gato se metió en la caja. "I'm dead"!

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.hook: ¡Se ha comido toda la pizza! "pig out".
l1.ex: Anoche hicimos "pig out" comiendo pizza.

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: Pizza a las seis, ¿trato? "bet".
l1.ex: ¿Pizza a las seis? "bet".

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: ¿Otra vez pizza y película? Tan "basic".
l1.ex: Mi plan de fin de semana es "basic": pizza y una película.

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: Esos dos dejaron de hablarse. ¿Tienen algún "beef"?
l1.ex: Ellos tienen "beef" por un juego.

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: ¡Tu habitación parece de Pinterest! Muy "aesthetic".
l1.ex: Tu escritorio se ve tan "aesthetic".

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.hook: ¡Papá vio la habitación desordenada! Va a hacer "blow a fuse".
l1.ex: Él hizo "blow a fuse" por la habitación desordenada.

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: ¡La pasta de mamá está increíble esta noche! Está "bussin".
l1.ex: La pasta de mamá está "bussin" esta noche.

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: ¡Muchas gracias por el viaje!
l1.ex: ¡Gracias por el viaje! "anytime".

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: ¡Cinco minutos y vuelvo!
l1.ex: Vuelvo pronto, estaré "AFK" cinco minutos.

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: ¿Dónde se fue la llave?
l1.ex: ¿Dónde está la llave? "beats me".

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: El plan falló. ¿Y ahora qué?
l1.ex: El plan falló. "back to square one".

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: ¡Mira el precio de este abrigo!
l1.ex: Este abrigo cuesta "arm and a leg".

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: ¡Oh, by the way, una cosa más!
l1.ex: By the way, la fiesta empieza a las siete.

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: ¿Conseguiste entradas gratis? ¡awesome!
l1.ex: ¿Conseguiste entradas gratis? ¡Eso es awesome!

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: Gato soñoliento. ¡big mood!
l1.ex: Ese gato soñoliento es un big mood.

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: Fin de semana lluvioso. Toda la temporada. ¡binge-watch!
l1.ex: Voy a binge-watch esta serie todo el fin de semana.

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: ¡Demasiado trabajo. Estoy 'burned out'!
l1.ex: Después de los exámenes, me sentí totalmente 'burned out'.

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: La semana pasada enfermo, ¡hoy estoy 'back on my feet'!
l1.ex: Finalmente estoy 'back on my feet'.

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: ¡Lo necesito ahora, 'ASAP'!
l1.ex: Por favor, envíame las notas 'ASAP'.

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: ¿Película esta noche a las seis, 'cool'?
l1.ex: Cool, nos vemos a las seis.

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: ¡Él nunca paga la comida! Es muy 'cheap'.
l1.ex: Él es demasiado 'cheap' para comprar la comida.

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.hook: Día de entrevista. ¡Traje y corbata para ir "dressed to impress"!
l1.ex: Él está "dressed to impress" para la entrevista.

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.hook: Dos horas de las mismas diapositivas, estoy "bored stiff".
l1.ex: Yo estaba "bored stiff" en esa clase.

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.hook: Sábado. ¿Dieta? ¿Qué dieta? Hoy es mi "cheat day".
l1.ex: El sábado es mi "cheat day".

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.hook: ¿Quién conoce todos tus secretos? Tu "bestie".
l1.ex: Mi "bestie" y yo amamos los tacos.

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.hook: ¿Aprobaste el examen? ¡big W!
l1.ex: ¿Aprobaste el examen? ¡Big W!

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.hook: ¡hot take! La pizza con piña es la mejor.
l1.ex: Aquí va mi hot take: la piña pertenece a la pizza.

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: ¡blooper! Se tropezó en la obra escolar.
l1.ex: Ese blooper hizo reír a toda la clase.

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.hook: ¿Cuánto costará? Dame una "ballpark figure".
l1.ex: Dame un "ballpark figure".

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.hook: Noche de juegos en mi casa, "count me in".
l1.ex: ¿Noche de juegos? ¡count me in!

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.hook: ¡Pon esta canción más alta!
l1.ex: ¡Esta nueva canción es un "banger"!

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

l1.hook: ¿Calcetines con sandalias? ¿En serio?
l1.ex: ¿Calcetines con sandalias? "big yikes".

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

l1.hook: Luces del escenario encendidas. ¡Mi mente está en blanco!
l1.ex: Me quedé "blank out" en medio de mi discurso.

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

l1.hook: ¡Tres horas de videos tontos!
l1.ex: Demasiados videos me dan "brain rot".

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

l1.hook: ¡No tengo tiempo libre esta semana!
l1.ex: Estoy "busy as a bee" esta semana.

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

l1.hook: Hace mucho frío afuera. ¿Listos para 'bundle up'?
l1.ex: ¡'Bundle up', hace mucho frío afuera!

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

l1.hook: No hay tiempo ahora. ¿'Circle back' más tarde?
l1.ex: Vamos a 'circle back' a eso después del almuerzo.

facts.def: Used to accept someone's point.

example.text: Fair enough, let's try your idea.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fair enough' to a rude insult.
misuse.why: It sounds like you agree with them.

l1.hook: ¡Espera, escucha mi razonamiento primero! "fair enough"
l1.ex: Fair enough, probemos tu idea.

facts.def: Describes things that are corny or too sweet.

example.text: That movie was so cheesy.

misuse.text: Don't call her poem 'cheesy' at the party.
misuse.why: It sounds mean about heartfelt effort.

l1.hook: Su nota de amor rima. ¡Qué 'cheesy'!
l1.ex: Esa película fue muy 'cheesy'.

facts.def: To answer criticism quickly and cleverly.

example.text: She clapped back with a great reply.

misuse.text: Don't 'clap back' at a parent's advice.

l1.hook: Él se burló de ella. ¡Ella le dio un "clap back"!
l1.ex: Ella hizo un "clap back" con una gran respuesta.

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

l1.hook: ¡Nueva chaqueta, nuevos zapatos, nueva confianza! "drip"
l1.ex: Buena chaqueta, hoy tienes "drip".

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: Viaje cancelado. Todos están "bummed out".
l1.ex: Estoy "bummed out" por el viaje.

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

l1.hook: ¡Prueba esto y dime! "chef's kiss"
l1.ex: La sopa estuvo "chef's kiss".

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

l1.hook: ¡Gracias por salvar mi tarea, "bro"!
l1.ex: ¡Gracias, "bro", me salvaste!

facts.def: To lead a team to victory with great skill.

example.text: Mia carried us in the final round.

misuse.text: Don't say 'she carried us' about a lazy teammate.
misuse.why: It praises someone who did the work.

l1.hook: ¡Ella ganó el partido sola!
l1.ex: Mia "carry" nos ayudó a ganar en la ronda final.

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

l1.hook: «Just kidding», dije mientras le decía: «¡Me comí tu pastel!»
l1.ex: ¡Me comí tu pastel! "just kidding".

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

l1.hook: Se me olvidaron los apuntes. ¡Estoy 'cooked'!
l1.ex: Olvidé mis apuntes. Estoy "cooked".

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

l1.hook: ¡Ella solo bebe té elegante!
l1.ex: Esta cafetería es muy "bougie".

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

l1.hook: ¿Quieres ir al espectáculo nocturno? 'Count me out'.
l1.ex: Estoy cansado, así que "count me out".

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: Él agradeció a todos, incluso a los rivales. ¡Qué 'class act'!
l1.ex: Nuestro entrenador es un verdadero "class act".

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: ¿Olvidaste la tarea otra vez? ¡'Bruh'!
l1.ex: "Bruh", ¿olvidaste la tarea otra vez?

facts.mean: A title that tricks you to click.
facts.def: A catchy headline that isn't worth reading.

example.text: That title is pure clickbait.

misuse.text: Don't call a real news story 'clickbait'.

l1.hook: «¡No lo vas a creer!» ¿En serio? 'clickbait'.
l1.ex: Ese título es puro "clickbait".

facts.def: To decide to finish work or an activity for now.

example.text: We're tired, let's call it a day.

misuse.text: Don't 'call it a day' before the deadline.

l1.hook: Estamos cansados. ¿Qué hacemos ahora? 'call it a day'.
l1.ex: Estamos cansados, vamos a "call it a day".

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

l1.hook: ¡Solo una pequeña noticia!
l1.ex: FYI, la tienda cierra a las cinco.

facts.def: Used to say you accept an idea.

example.text: Pizza or tacos? Fine by me.
