misuse.text: Don't say 'fine by me' when you're upset.
misuse.why: People will think you truly don't mind.

l1.hook: ¿Pizza o tacos? Tú eliges?
l1.ex: ¿Pizza o tacos? "fine by me".

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

l1.hook: El juego de palabras de papá otra vez. ¿En serio?
l1.ex: Los chistes de papá son tan "corny".

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.hook: ¡El chat grupal explotó por nada!
l1.ex: No quiero "drama" este año.

facts.def: A moment to show your outfit and get opinions.

example.text: Quick fit check before school!

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'fit check' at the gym.

l1.hook: Conjunto listo. "fit check", ¿qué opinas antes de la escuela?
l1.ex: ¡Rápido "fit check" antes de la escuela!

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.hook: Se ve triste. "cheer up", ¿qué hacemos ahora?
l1.ex: ¡"Cheer up", vamos a comer pizza!

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.hook: ¿Día triste? Sopa caliente, "comfort food".
l1.ex: La sopa caliente es mi "comfort food".

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: ¿Quién estudia contigo cada noche, "buddy"?
l1.ex: Él es mi "buddy" de estudio.

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.hook: ¡Gol de último segundo que lo decide, "clutch"!
l1.ex: Ese gol de último minuto fue tan "clutch".

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: ¿Esta tienda es 'legit'?
l1.ex: Esta tienda es 'legit', mi hermana compró zapatos allí.

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

l1.hook: Soy nuevo, 'cut me some slack', por favor sé amable.
l1.ex: 'cut me some slack', soy nuevo.

facts.def: To cost so much that you can't afford it.

example.text: Don't worry, this lunch won't break the bank.

misuse.text: Don't say 'break the bank' at a bank.
misuse.why: It only means costing too much.

l1.hook: ¿El almuerzo va a 'break the bank'?
l1.ex: No te preocupes, este almuerzo no 'break the bank'.

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: Pasa cuando quieras esta semana, 'drop by'.
l1.ex: Siéntete libre de 'drop by' cuando quieras.

facts.def: Used when someone is doing really well at something.

example.text: You're crushing it at your new job!

misuse.text: Don't tell a struggling friend 'crushing it' sarcastically.

l1.hook: Primera semana y ya estás 'crushing it'.
l1.ex: Estás 'crushing it' en tu nuevo trabajo.

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: El viaje se canceló. ¡Qué "bummer"!
l1.ex: ¿Se canceló el viaje? Qué "bummer".

facts.def: To study many things quickly just before a test.

example.text: I must cram for math.

misuse.text: Don't 'cram' for a three-year course.
misuse.why: Cramming only works for short tests.

l1.hook: Examen mañana. ¡No he estudiado, "cram"!
l1.ex: Tengo que "cram" para matemáticas.

facts.mean: Scroll bad news for too long.
facts.def: To keep reading sad online news without stopping.

example.text: Stop doomscrolling and go to sleep.

misuse.text: Don't say 'doomscroll' about reading a recipe.

l1.m: desplazarse sin cesar por noticias deprimentes
l1.hook: Medianoche. Sigo haciendo doomscroll con noticias malas.
l1.ex: Deja de "doomscrolling" y ve a dormir.

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: Es tarde y tengo sueño. Necesito "catch some Zs".
l1.ex: Voy a "catch some Zs".

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

l1.hook: Una siesta, y estoy "good as new".
l1.ex: Después de una siesta, me siento "good as new".

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

l1.hook: Empieza la reunión. ¿Quién va a "get the ball rolling"?
l1.ex: Vamos a "get the ball rolling" con ideas.

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

l1.hook: ¿Puedo contar contigo? "for sure".
l1.ex: ¿Pizza esta noche? "for sure"!

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

l1.hook: La fiesta terminó a las ocho. ¡Qué "lame"!
l1.ex: Esa fiesta fue un poco "lame".

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

l1.hook: Sonreímos, pero competimos, como un "frenemy".
l1.ex: Ella es mi "frenemy", siempre compitiendo conmigo.

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: Ese abrigo parece de películas antiguas, "it's giving".
l1.ex: Ese abrigo está "it's giving" a estrella de película antigua.

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: Día difícil, pero "chin up", mañana llega.
l1.ex: "Chin up", mañana será mejor.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: La cena está lista. ¿Quién tiene hambre? "dig in"
l1.ex: La cena está lista, ¡así que "dig in"!

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: Tengo que irme. La clase empieza ahora. "catch you later"
l1.ex: "Catch you later", tengo que irme!

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: Gol de último segundo. ¡Ganamos! "epic win"
l1.ex: Anotamos en el último segundo. "Epic win"!

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

l1.hook: ¿Opinión honesta sobre esa película? "ngl"
l1.ex: "Ngl", me encantó esa película.

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: ¡Mi pastel se derrumbó! Todos lo vieron.
l1.ex: Mi pastel quedó plano. ¡Total "epic fail"!

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

l1.hook: ¿Regalo para ella? ¿Alguien?
l1.ex: Vamos a "chip in" todos para su regalo.

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: Examen mañana. ¿Por dónde empezamos?
l1.ex: Entonces, ¿cuál es el "game plan"?

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

l1.hook: ¡Mira mis nuevas zapatillas!
l1.ex: ¡Esas zapatillas son "fire"!

facts.def: A casual way to ask someone to repeat.

example.text: Come again? It's too loud here.

misuse.text: Don't say 'come again' when you heard clearly.

l1.hook: ¡Perdón, la música está demasiado alta!
l1.ex: ¿"Come again"? Está demasiado ruidoso aquí.

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

l1.hook: Exámenes finales la próxima semana. Es hora de "hit the books".
l1.ex: Tengo que "hit the books" esta noche.

facts.def: People who love the same show or band.

example.text: The fandom loves this band.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers a 'fandom'.
misuse.why: It means devoted fans of one thing.

l1.hook: ¿Quién ama más a esta banda? Hablemos del "fandom".
l1.ex: El "fandom" ama a esta banda.

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

l1.hook: ¡Esa caminata se sintió interminable! Estoy "dog tired".
l1.ex: Estoy "dog tired" después de esa larga caminata.

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: ¡Mira por la ventana! ¡Coge un paraguas! Está "raining cats and dogs".
l1.ex: ¡Está "raining cats and dogs"!

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

l1.hook: ¡Aviso rápido: el jefe viene! Aquí tienes un "heads up".
l1.ex: Solo una "heads up", la reunión empieza temprano.

facts.def: Used to say you agree to a plan or want to do it.

example.text: We're going bowling tonight. Are you down?

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm down' when you feel sad.
misuse.why: It can also mean feeling low.

l1.hook: ¿Vamos a jugar bolos esta noche? ¿Quién viene? "I'm down"
l1.ex: Vamos a jugar bolos esta noche. ¿Te apuntas? "I'm down"

facts.def: Used when something doesn't seem logical.

example.text: This game rule makes no sense.

misuse.text: Don't say 'makes no sense' about your boss's plan.

l1.hook: Las reglas cambiaron otra vez. ¿Por qué? "makes no sense"
l1.ex: Esta regla del juego "makes no sense".

facts.def: Something unfair said to hurt someone.

example.text: That joke was a low blow.

misuse.text: Don't call fair criticism a 'low blow'.
misuse.why: It may just be honest feedback.

l1.hook: ¡Él mencionó su error del pasado! "low blow"
l1.ex: Ese chiste fue un "low blow".

facts.mean: Succeed at wearing or doing something bold.
facts.def: To manage something hard or bold, like a style.

example.text: Not everyone can pull off that color.

misuse.text: Don't say 'pull off' when you mean 'remove'.

l1.hook: ¿Quién más lleva eso? "pull off"
l1.ex: No todos pueden "pull off" ese color.

facts.mean: Grumpy and in a bad mood.
facts.def: Describes someone tired or annoyed.

example.text: I'm cranky before breakfast.

misuse.text: Don't call your boss 'cranky' in an email.

l1.hook: ¡No me hables todavía! "cranky"
l1.ex: Estoy "cranky" antes del desayuno.

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: Meilleure pizza de la ville. Crois-moi, no cap.
l1.ex: Cette pizza est la meilleure de la ville, no cap.

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: Il a perdu, puis il s’est morfondu, salty.
l1.ex: Il est salty parce que j’ai gagné au jeu de cartes.

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: Le chat a sauté dans la boîte ! I'm dead.
l1.ex: Le chat a sauté dans la boîte. I'm dead !

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.hook: Toute la pizza a disparu ! « pig out »
l1.ex: On a « pigged out » sur de la pizza hier soir.

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: Pizza à six heures, d’accord ? bet.
l1.ex: Pizza à six heures ? Bet.

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: Pizza et un film encore ? C’est tellement "basic".
l1.ex: Mon plan de week‑end est "basic" : pizza et un film.

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: Ces deux‑là ont arrêté de parler. C’est à cause du "beef".
l1.ex: Ils ont du "beef" à propos d'un jeu.

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: Ta chambre a un style "aesthetic" comme sur Pinterest !
l1.ex: Ton bureau est tellement "aesthetic".

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.hook: Papa a vu la chambre en désordre ! « blow a fuse »
l1.ex: Il a « blown a fuse » à cause de la chambre en désordre.

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: Les pâtes de maman sont « bussin » ce soir !
l1.ex: Les pâtes de maman sont "bussin" ce soir.

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: Merci beaucoup pour le trajet ! « anytime »
l1.ex: Merci pour le trajet ! "anytime".

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: Cinq minutes, puis je reviens ! « AFK »
l1.ex: Je reviens tout de suite, je serai "AFK" pendant cinq minutes.

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: Où est passée la clé ? « beats me ».
l1.ex: Où est la clé ? "Beats me".

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: Le plan a échoué. Et maintenant ? « back to square one ».
l1.ex: Le plan a échoué. "Back to square one".

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.m: coûter les yeux de la tête
l1.hook: Regarde le prix de ce manteau ! « arm and a leg ».
l1.ex: Ce manteau coûte "arm and a leg".

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: Oh, « by the way », une autre chose !
l1.ex: « By the way », la fête commence à sept heures.

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: Tu as eu des billets gratuits pour nous ? « awesome »
l1.ex: Tu as eu des billets gratuits pour nous ? C’est « awesome » !

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: Chat endormi. Exactement mon « big mood » !
l1.ex: Ce chat endormi est un « big mood ».

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.hook: Jour de test. Comment ça s’est passé ? « ace »
l1.ex: J'ai « aced » mon contrôle d'histoire aujourd'hui !

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: Week-end pluvieux. Toute la saison. Allez, « binge-watch » !
l1.ex: Je vais « binge-watch » cette série tout le week-end.

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: Trop de travail. Je suis « burned out ».
l1.ex: Après les examens, je me suis senti totalement « burned out ».

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: La semaine dernière j'étais malade, aujourd'hui je suis « back on my feet ».
l1.ex: Je suis enfin « back on my feet ».

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: J'en ai besoin tout de suite, « ASAP » !
l1.ex: Veuillez m'envoyer les notes « ASAP ».

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: Film ce soir à six heures, « cool » ?
l1.ex: « Cool », à six heures !

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: Il ne paie jamais le déjeuner, il est « cheap ».
l1.ex: Il est trop « cheap » pour acheter le déjeuner.

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.hook: Elle a dit à tout le monde mon erreur ! « call out »
l1.ex: Elle m'a « called out » parce que j'étais en retard.

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.hook: Jour d'entretien. Costume et cravate ! "dressed to impress"
l1.ex: Il est "dressed to impress" pour l'entretien.

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.hook: Deux heures des mêmes diapositives ! "bored stiff"
l1.ex: J'étais "bored stiff" dans ce cours.

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.hook: Samedi. Régime ? Quel régime ? "cheat day"
l1.ex: Samedi, c'est mon "cheat day".

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.hook: Qui connaît tous tes secrets ? "bestie"
l1.ex: Mon "bestie" et moi aimons les tacos.

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.hook: Tu as réussi le test ? Wow ! « big W ».
l1.ex: Tu as réussi le test ? "Big W" !

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.hook: La pizza à l'ananas est la meilleure ! « hot take ».
l1.ex: Voici mon « hot take » : l'ananas appartient à la pizza.

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: Il a trébuché dans la pièce de théâtre scolaire ! « blooper ».
l1.ex: Ce "blooper" a fait rire toute la classe.

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.hook: Combien cela coûtera-t-il ? "ballpark figure"
l1.ex: Donne-moi une "ballpark figure".

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.hook: Soirée jeux chez moi ! "count me in"
l1.ex: Soirée jeux ? "Count me in" !

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.hook: Fais monter le son de cette chanson ! "banger"
l1.ex: Cette nouvelle chanson est un "banger" !

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

l1.hook: Des chaussettes avec des sandales ? Vraiment ? "big yikes"
l1.ex: Des chaussettes avec des sandales ? "Big yikes".

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

l1.hook: Les lumières de la scène sont allumées. Mon esprit est vide ! "blank out"
l1.ex: J'ai eu un "blank out" au milieu de mon discours.

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

l1.hook: Trois heures de vidéos stupides ! "brain rot"
l1.ex: Trop de vidéos me donnent du "brain rot".

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

l1.hook: Pas de temps libre cette semaine ! "busy as a bee"
l1.ex: Je suis "busy as a bee" cette semaine.

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

l1.hook: Il fait un froid glacial dehors. Prêt à "bundle up" ?
l1.ex: "Bundle up", il fait un froid glacial dehors !

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

l1.hook: Pas de temps maintenant. On "circle back" plus tard ?
l1.ex: On "circle back" à ça après le déjeuner.

facts.def: Used to accept someone's point.

example.text: Fair enough, let's try your idea.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fair enough' to a rude insult.
misuse.why: It sounds like you agree with them.

l1.hook: Attends, écoute mon raisonnement d'abord !
l1.ex: « fair enough », essayons ton idée.

facts.def: Describes things that are corny or too sweet.

example.text: That movie was so cheesy.

misuse.text: Don't call her poem 'cheesy' at the party.
misuse.why: It sounds mean about heartfelt effort.

l1.hook: Sa note d'amour rimait. Beurk !
l1.ex: Ce film était tellement « cheesy ».

facts.def: To answer criticism quickly and cleverly.

example.text: She clapped back with a great reply.

misuse.text: Don't 'clap back' at a parent's advice.

l1.hook: Il s'est moqué d'elle. Elle a répliqué !
l1.ex: Elle a « clap back » avec une super réponse.

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

l1.hook: Nouvelle veste, nouvelles chaussures, nouvelle confiance !
l1.ex: Belle veste, tu as du « drip » aujourd'hui.

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: Voyage annulé. Tout le monde est triste !
l1.ex: Je suis « bummed out » à propos du voyage.

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

l1.hook: Goûte ça et dis‑moi, c’est un "chef's kiss" !
l1.ex: La soupe était « chef's kiss ».

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

l1.hook: Merci d'avoir sauvé mon devoir, "bro" !
l1.ex: Merci, bro, tu m'as sauvé !

facts.def: To lead a team to victory with great skill.

example.text: Mia carried us in the final round.

misuse.text: Don't say 'she carried us' about a lazy teammate.
misuse.why: It praises someone who did the work.

l1.hook: Elle a gagné le match toute seule !
l1.ex: Mia nous a « carry » lors du dernier round.

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

l1.hook: J’ai mangé ton gâteau, "just kidding" !
l1.ex: J'ai mangé ton gâteau ! Just kidding.

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

l1.hook: J’ai oublié mes notes. "cooked" !
l1.ex: J'ai oublié mes notes. Je suis « cooked ».

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

l1.hook: Elle ne boit que du thé "bougie" !
l1.ex: Ce café est tellement "bougie".

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

l1.hook: Tu veux aller au spectacle tardif ? "count me out"
l1.ex: Je suis fatigué, alors "count me out".

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: Il a remercié tout le monde, même les rivaux, c’est un vrai "class act".
l1.ex: Notre entraîneur est un vrai "class act".

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: Tu as encore oublié tes devoirs ? "bruh" !
l1.ex: "Bruh", tu as encore oublié tes devoirs ?

facts.def: To keep working late into the night.

example.text: We burned the midnight oil last night.

misuse.text: Don't say it about lighting candles.

l1.hook: Tu travailles encore à 2h du matin ? "burn the midnight oil".
l1.ex: Nous avons « burn the midnight oil » hier soir.

facts.mean: A title that tricks you to click.
facts.def: A catchy headline that isn't worth reading.

example.text: That title is pure clickbait.

misuse.text: Don't call a real news story 'clickbait'.

l1.hook: « Vous ne le croirez pas ! » Vraiment ?
l1.ex: Ce titre est du pur "clickbait".

facts.def: To decide to finish work or an activity for now.

example.text: We're tired, let's call it a day.

misuse.text: Don't 'call it a day' before the deadline.

l1.hook: Nous sommes fatigués. Et maintenant ?
l1.ex: Nous sommes fatigués, on va "call it a day".

facts.def: To begin to feel ill with something like a cold.

example.text: I think I'm coming down with a cold.

misuse.text: Don't say you 'came down with' a gift.
misuse.why: It means starting to get sick.

l1.hook: J’ai mal à la gorge. Oups !
l1.ex: Je pense que je suis en train de « come down with » un rhume.

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

l1.hook: Juste une petite nouvelle !
l1.ex: "FYI", le magasin ferme à cinq heures.

facts.def: Used to say you accept an idea.

example.text: Pizza or tacos? Fine by me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fine by me' when you're upset.
misuse.why: People will think you truly don't mind.

l1.hook: Pizza ou tacos, à toi de choisir ?
l1.ex: Pizza ou tacos ? "fine by me".

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

l1.hook: Le jeu de mots de papa encore. Sérieusement ? "corny".
l1.ex: Les blagues de papa sont tellement "corny".

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.hook: Le groupe de discussion a explosé pour rien, quel "drama" !
l1.ex: Je ne veux pas de "drama" cette année.

facts.def: A moment to show your outfit and get opinions.

example.text: Quick fit check before school!

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'fit check' at the gym.

l1.hook: C’est un "fit check" : tenue prête. Qu’en penses‑tu avant l’école ?
l1.ex: Vérification rapide de "fit check" avant l'école !

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.hook: Elle a l'air triste. "Cheer up" ! Que faire maintenant ?
l1.ex: "Cheer up", on mange de la pizza !

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.hook: Journée triste ? "Comfort food" : soupe chaude !
l1.ex: La soupe chaude est mon "comfort food".

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: Qui est ton "buddy" qui étudie avec toi chaque nuit ?
l1.ex: C’est mon "buddy" d’études.

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.hook: But de dernière seconde qui fait gagner le match ! "clutch"
l1.ex: Ce but de dernière minute était tellement "clutch".

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: Ce magasin est‑il "legit" ?
l1.ex: Ce magasin est "legit", ma sœur y a acheté des chaussures.

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

l1.hook: Je suis nouveau. "Cut me some slack", s'il te plaît !
l1.ex: "Cut me some slack", je suis nouveau.

facts.def: To cost so much that you can't afford it.

example.text: Don't worry, this lunch won't break the bank.

misuse.text: Don't say 'break the bank' at a bank.
misuse.why: It only means costing too much.

l1.hook: Le déjeuner est-il trop cher ? "break the bank"
l1.ex: Ne t'inquiète pas, ce déjeuner ne va pas "break the bank".

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: N'hésite pas à "drop by" n'importe quand cette semaine ?
l1.ex: N'hésite pas à "drop by" quand tu veux.

facts.def: Used when someone is doing really well at something.

example.text: You're crushing it at your new job!

misuse.text: Don't tell a struggling friend 'crushing it' sarcastically.

l1.hook: Première semaine, déjà meilleur vendeur!
l1.ex: Tu « crushing it » dans ton nouveau travail !

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: Le voyage a été annulé. "Bummer" !
l1.ex: Le voyage est annulé ? Quel "bummer".

facts.def: To study many things quickly just before a test.

example.text: I must cram for math.

misuse.text: Don't 'cram' for a three-year course.
misuse.why: Cramming only works for short tests.

l1.hook: Examen demain. Je n'ai pas étudié ! Il faut « cram ».
l1.ex: Je dois "cram" pour les maths.

facts.mean: Scroll bad news for too long.
facts.def: To keep reading sad online news without stopping.

example.text: Stop doomscrolling and go to sleep.

misuse.text: Don't say 'doomscroll' about reading a recipe.

l1.hook: Minuit. Je continue de « doomscroll » les mauvaises nouvelles !
l1.ex: Arrête de « doomscroll » et va dormir.

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: Il se fait tard et je suis fatigué, je vais "catch some Zs".
l1.ex: Je vais "catch some Zs".

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

l1.hook: Une sieste, et je suis "good as new".
l1.ex: Après une sieste, je me sens "good as new".

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

l1.hook: La réunion commence. Qui va "get the ball rolling" ?
l1.ex: Allons-y, "get the ball rolling" avec des idées.

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

l1.hook: Puis-je compter sur toi ? "for sure"
l1.ex: Pizza ce soir ? "for sure" !

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

l1.hook: La fête s'est terminée à huit heures. Sérieusement, c'est "lame".
l1.ex: Cette fête était un peu "lame".

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

l1.hook: On sourit, mais on se fait concurrence, comme des "frenemy" !
l1.ex: C’est ma "frenemy", toujours en compétition avec moi.

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: Ce manteau ressemble à ceux des vieux films ! "it's giving"
l1.ex: Ce manteau donne l'impression d'une star de vieux films. "it's giving"

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: Journée difficile, mais demain arrive, alors "chin up" !
l1.ex: "Chin up", demain sera meilleur.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: Le dîner est prêt. Qui a faim ? "dig in"
l1.ex: Le dîner est prêt, alors "dig in" !

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: Je dois filer, le cours commence, "catch you later" !
l1.ex: "Catch you later", je dois y aller !

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: But de dernière seconde. Nous gagnons ! "epic win"
l1.ex: On a marqué à la dernière seconde. « epic win » !

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

l1.hook: Quel est ton avis honnête sur ce film ? « ngl »
l1.ex: « ngl », j’ai adoré ce film.

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: Mon gâteau s’est effondré. Tout le monde a regardé ! « epic fail »
l1.ex: Mon gâteau est tombé à plat. Total « epic fail » !

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

l1.m: mettre la main à la poche
l1.hook: Cadeau pour elle ? Qui veut « chip in » ?
l1.ex: Allons tous « chip in » pour son cadeau.

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: Test demain. Par où commencer ? « game plan »
l1.ex: Alors, quel est le « game plan » ?

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

l1.hook: Regarde mes nouvelles baskets ! Elles sont "fire".
l1.ex: Ces baskets sont "fire" !

facts.def: A casual way to ask someone to repeat.

example.text: Come again? It's too loud here.

misuse.text: Don't say 'come again' when you heard clearly.

l1.hook: Désolé, la musique est trop forte ! "Come again" ?
l1.ex: "Come again" ? Il y a trop de bruit ici.

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

l1.hook: Les partiels sont la semaine prochaine. C’est la panique ! Il faut "hit the books".
l1.ex: Je dois "hit the books" ce soir.

facts.def: People who love the same show or band.

example.text: The fandom loves this band.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers a 'fandom'.
misuse.why: It means devoted fans of one thing.

l1.hook: Qui aime le plus ce groupe ? "Fandom" ?
l1.ex: "Fandom" adore ce groupe.

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

l1.hook: Cette randonnée était interminable ! Je suis "dog tired".
l1.ex: Je suis "dog tired" après cette longue randonnée.

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: Regarde dehors ! Prends un parapluie ! "raining cats and dogs"
l1.ex: Il pleut « raining cats and dogs »!

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

l1.hook: Petit avertissement : le patron arrive ! "heads up"
l1.ex: Just a heads up, la réunion commence tôt.

facts.def: Used to say you agree to a plan or want to do it.

example.text: We're going bowling tonight. Are you down?

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm down' when you feel sad.
misuse.why: It can also mean feeling low.

l1.hook: Bowling ce soir, qui vient ? "I'm down"
l1.ex: Nous allons faire du bowling ce soir. Tu es partant ? "I'm down"

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: शहर की सबसे बेहतरीन पिज़्ज़ा है, "no cap"। विश्वास करो?
l1.ex: यह पिज़्ज़ा शहर की सबसे बेहतरीन है, "no cap"।

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: वह हार गया, फिर "salty" हो गया!
l1.ex: मैंने कार्ड गेम जीता, इसलिए वह "salty" है।

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: "I'm dead"—बिल्ली बॉक्स में कूद गई!
l1.ex: बिल्ली बॉक्स में कूद गई। "I'm dead"।

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.hook: "pig out"—पूरी पिज़्ज़ा खत्म हो गई!
l1.ex: हमने कल रात पिज़्ज़ा पर "pig out" किया।

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: छह बजे पिज़्ज़ा, bet?
l1.ex: छह बजे पिज़्ज़ा? "bet"।

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: फिर पिज़्ज़ा और फिल्म, basic?
l1.ex: मेरी वीकेंड योजना basic है: पिज़्ज़ा और फ़िल्म।

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: वो दोनों बात करना बंद कर गए। क्यों? beef?
l1.ex: उनके बीच खेल को लेकर beef है।

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: तुम्हारा कमरा Pinterest जैसा दिख रहा है! aesthetic
l1.ex: तुम्हारी डेस्क बहुत aesthetic लग रही है।

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.hook: पिता ने गंदा कमरा देखा! blow a fuse
l1.ex: उसने गंदे कमरे को देखकर blow a fuse कर दिया।

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: माँ की पास्ता आज रात "bussin" है!
l1.ex: माँ की पास्ता आज रात bussin है।

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: सवारी के लिए बहुत धन्यवाद! "anytime"
l1.ex: सवारी के लिए धन्यवाद! "anytime"

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: पाँच मिनट, फिर मैं वापस आऊँगा! "AFK"
l1.ex: ब्रेक ले रहा हूँ, मैं पाँच मिनट के लिए AFK रहूँगा।

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: चाबी कहाँ गई? "beats me"
l1.ex: चाबी कहाँ है? "beats me"

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: योजना विफल हो गई। अब क्या? "back to square one"
l1.ex: योजना विफल हो गई। "back to square one"

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: इस कोट की कीमत देखो! "arm and a leg"
l1.ex: इस कोट की कीमत "arm and a leg" है।

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: by the way, एक बात और!
l1.ex: by the way, पार्टी सात बजे शुरू होती है।

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: क्या तुम्हें हमारे लिए मुफ्त टिकट मिल गए? awesome
l1.ex: तुम्हारे पास हमारे लिए मुफ्त टिकट हैं? That's awesome!

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: नींद वाली बिल्ली—बिल्कुल मेरा "big mood"!
l1.ex: वह नींद वाली बिल्ली एक big mood है।

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.hook: परीक्षा का दिन। तुमने कैसे 'ace' किया?
l1.ex: मैंने आज अपना इतिहास टेस्ट ace किया!

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: बारिश वाला सप्ताहांत। पूरी सीज़न 'binge-watch' करो! चलो!
l1.ex: मैं इस शो को पूरे वीकेंड binge-watch करूँगा।

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: बहुत काम, मैं 'burned out' हूँ!
l1.ex: परीक्षाओं के बाद, मैं पूरी तरह 'burned out' महसूस किया।

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: पिछले हफ्ते बीमार था, आज मैं 'back on my feet' हूँ!
l1.ex: मैं अंततः 'back on my feet' हूँ।

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: मुझे यह अभी चाहिए, 'ASAP'!
l1.ex: कृपया नोट्स मुझे 'ASAP' भेजें।

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: आज रात छह बजे फिल्म, ठीक है? 'cool'।
l1.ex: 'cool', छह बजे मिलते हैं!

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: वह कभी लंच का भुगतान नहीं करता, वह 'cheap' है!
l1.ex: वह लंच खरीदने के लिए बहुत 'cheap' है।

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.hook: उसने सबको मेरी गलती 'call out' कर दी!
l1.ex: उसने मुझे देर से आने के लिए "call out" किया।

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.hook: इंटरव्यू का दिन। सूट और टाई, 'dressed to impress'!
l1.ex: वह इंटरव्यू के लिए "dressed to impress" कपड़े पहने है।

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.hook: दो घंटे एक ही स्लाइड्स, मैं "bored stiff" हूँ!
l1.ex: मैं उस क्लास में "bored stiff" था।

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.hook: शनिवार। डाइट? कौन सी डाइट? बिल्कुल 'cheat day'!
l1.ex: शनिवार मेरा "cheat day" है।

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.hook: कौन तुम्हारे सभी राज़ जानता है? बिल्कुल 'bestie'!
l1.ex: मेरी "bestie" और मैं टैकोस पसंद करते हैं।

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.hook: तुमने टेस्ट पास कर लिया? "big W"!
l1.ex: तुमने टेस्ट पास कर लिया? "Big W"!

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.hook: अनानास पिज़्ज़ा सबसे अच्छा है! यह एक 'hot take' है!
l1.ex: यहाँ मेरा "hot take": पाइनएप्पल पिज़्ज़ा पर होना चाहिए।

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: वह स्कूल नाटक में ठोकर खा गया! यह एक 'blooper' है!
l1.ex: वह "blooper" पूरी कक्षा को हँसा दिया।

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.hook: यह कितना खर्च होगा? एक "ballpark figure" बताइए।
l1.ex: मुझे "ballpark figure" दो।

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.hook: मेरे घर पर गेम नाइट, "count me in"!
l1.ex: गेम नाइट? "count me in"!

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.hook: इस गाने को ज़्यादा तेज़ चलाओ!
l1.ex: यह नया गाना एक "banger" है!

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

l1.hook: सैंडल के साथ मोज़े? सच में?
l1.ex: सैंडल के साथ मोज़े? "big yikes".

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

l1.hook: स्टेज़ की लाइटें ऑन हैं। मेरा दिमाग खाली है!
l1.ex: मैं अपने भाषण के बीच में "blank out" हो गया।

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

l1.hook: तीन घंटे की बेतुकी वीडियो!
l1.ex: बहुत सारी वीडियो मुझे "brain rot" देती हैं।

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

l1.hook: इस हफ़्ते कोई खाली समय नहीं है!
l1.ex: मैं इस हफ़्ते "busy as a bee" हूँ।

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

l1.hook: बाहर बहुत ठंड है, तैयार हो? "bundle up"
l1.ex: "bundle up", बाहर बहुत ठंड है!

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

l1.hook: अब समय नहीं है, बाद में? "circle back"
l1.ex: "circle back" चलिए दोपहर के बाद उस पर वापस आते हैं।

facts.def: Used to accept someone's point.

example.text: Fair enough, let's try your idea.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fair enough' to a rude insult.
misuse.why: It sounds like you agree with them.

l1.hook: रुको, पहले मेरी वजह सुनो! "fair enough"
l1.ex: "fair enough", चलो तुम्हारा विचार आज़माते हैं।

facts.def: Describes things that are corny or too sweet.

example.text: That movie was so cheesy.

misuse.text: Don't call her poem 'cheesy' at the party.
misuse.why: It sounds mean about heartfelt effort.

l1.hook: उसका प्रेम पत्र तुकबंदी वाला था। उफ़! "cheesy"
l1.ex: वह फिल्म बहुत "cheesy" थी।

facts.def: To answer criticism quickly and cleverly.

example.text: She clapped back with a great reply.

misuse.text: Don't 'clap back' at a parent's advice.

l1.hook: उसने उसकी मजाक उड़ाया। उसने जवाब दिया! "clap back"
l1.ex: "clap back" उसने एक शानदार जवाब दिया।

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

l1.hook: नई जैकेट, नए जूते, नया आत्मविश्वास! "drip"
l1.ex: अच्छी जैकेट, आज तुम्हारे पास 'drip' है।

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: यात्रा रद्द हो गई। सब 'bummed out' हैं।
l1.ex: मैं यात्रा के बारे में 'bummed out' हूँ।

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

l1.hook: इसे चखो और बताओ, यह 'chef's kiss' है।
l1.ex: सूप 'chef's kiss' था।

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

l1.hook: धन्यवाद, 'bro', मेरे होमवर्क को बचाने के लिए!
l1.ex: धन्यवाद, 'bro', तुमने मेरी मदद की।

facts.def: To lead a team to victory with great skill.

example.text: Mia carried us in the final round.

misuse.text: Don't say 'she carried us' about a lazy teammate.
misuse.why: It praises someone who did the work.

l1.hook: उसने अकेले ही मैच जीत कर टीम को 'carry' किया।
l1.ex: मिया ने फाइनल राउंड में हमें 'carry' किया।

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

l1.hook: मैंने तुम्हारा केक खा लिया!
l1.ex: मैंने तुम्हारा केक खा लिया। Just kidding.

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

l1.hook: मैंने अपने नोट्स भूल गया। Uh-oh!
l1.ex: मैंने अपने नोट्स भूल गया। I'm cooked.

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

l1.hook: वह केवल महँचा चाय पीती है!
l1.ex: यह कॉफ़ी शॉप बहुत bougie है।

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

l1.hook: क्या तुम देर की शो में जाना चाहते हो?
l1.ex: मैं थका हुआ हूँ, इसलिए count me out।

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: उसने सभी का धन्यवाद किया, यहाँ तक कि प्रतिद्वंद्वियों का भी!
l1.ex: हमारा कोच एक असली class act है।

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: Bruh, तुमने फिर से अपना होमवर्क भूल गया?
l1.ex: Bruh, तुमने फिर से अपना होमवर्क भूल गया?

facts.def: To keep working late into the night.

example.text: We burned the midnight oil last night.

misuse.text: Don't say it about lighting candles.

l1.hook: अभी भी दो बजे रात को "burn the midnight oil" कर रहे हो?
l1.ex: हमने कल रात "burn the midnight oil" किया।

facts.mean: A title that tricks you to click.
facts.def: A catchy headline that isn't worth reading.

example.text: That title is pure clickbait.

misuse.text: Don't call a real news story 'clickbait'.

l1.hook: 'तुम विश्वास नहीं करोगे!' सच में? यह 'clickbait' है।
l1.ex: वह शीर्षक पूरी तरह "clickbait" है।

facts.def: To decide to finish work or an activity for now.

example.text: We're tired, let's call it a day.

misuse.text: Don't 'call it a day' before the deadline.

l1.m: आज के लिए काम समाप्त करो
l1.hook: हम थक गए हैं। अब क्या? "call it a day"?
l1.ex: हम थक गए हैं, चलो "call it a day" करते हैं।

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

l1.hook: बस थोड़ी ख़बर!
l1.ex: FYI, दुकान पाँच बजे बंद हो जाती है।

facts.def: Used to say you accept an idea.

example.text: Pizza or tacos? Fine by me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fine by me' when you're upset.
misuse.why: People will think you truly don't mind.

l1.hook: पिज़्ज़ा या टैकोस, तुम चुनो?
l1.ex: पिज़्ज़ा या टैकोस? "fine by me"।

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

l1.hook: पिता की फिर से पन। सच में?
l1.ex: पिता के चुटकुले बहुत "corny" हैं।

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.hook: ग्रुप चैट में कुछ नहीं पर झगड़ा हो गया!
l1.ex: मैं इस साल कोई "drama" नहीं चाहता।

facts.def: A moment to show your outfit and get opinions.

example.text: Quick fit check before school!

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'fit check' at the gym.

l1.hook: पहनावा तैयार। स्कूल से पहले क्या सोचते हो?
l1.ex: जल्दी "fit check" स्कूल से पहले!

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.hook: वह उदास दिख रही है। अब क्या? चलो 'cheer up' करें।
l1.ex: Cheer up, हम पिज़्ज़ा खा रहे हैं!

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.hook: उदास दिन? गर्म सूप! यह 'comfort food' है।
l1.ex: गरम सूप मेरा "comfort food" है।

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: रात‑रात तुम्हारे साथ पढ़ने वाला "buddy" कौन है?
l1.ex: वह मेरा पढ़ाई का "buddy" है।

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.m: ऐन मौके पर काम आने वाला
l1.hook: आख़िरी सेकंड में गोल करने वाला "clutch" जीतता है!
l1.ex: वह आखिरी मिनट का गोल बहुत "clutch" था।

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: क्या यह दुकान "legit" है?
l1.ex: यह दुकान "legit" है, मेरी बहन ने वहाँ जूते खरीदे थे।

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

l1.hook: मैं नया हूँ, कृपया "cut me some slack"।
l1.ex: "Cut me some slack", मैं नया हूँ।

facts.def: To cost so much that you can't afford it.

example.text: Don't worry, this lunch won't break the bank.

misuse.text: Don't say 'break the bank' at a bank.
misuse.why: It only means costing too much.

l1.hook: क्या दोपहर का खाना बहुत महँगा है?
l1.ex: चिंता मत करो, यह लंच "break the bank" नहीं होगा।

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: इस हफ़्ते कभी भी "drop by" आ सकते हैं!
l1.ex: कभी भी "drop by" करने में संकोच न करें।

facts.def: Used when someone is doing really well at something.

example.text: You're crushing it at your new job!

misuse.text: Don't tell a struggling friend 'crushing it' sarcastically.

l1.hook: पहले हफ़्ते में ही आप "crushing it" हैं, टॉप सेलर!
l1.ex: आप "crushing it" कर रहे हैं अपने नए काम में!

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: यात्रा रद्द हो गई, "bummer"!
l1.ex: यात्रा रद्द हो गई? क्या "bummer"।

facts.def: To study many things quickly just before a test.

example.text: I must cram for math.

misuse.text: Don't 'cram' for a three-year course.
misuse.why: Cramming only works for short tests.

l1.hook: कल परीक्षा है, मैंने अभी तक पढ़ाई नहीं की! "cram" करो!
l1.ex: मुझे गणित के लिए "cram" करना है।

facts.mean: Scroll bad news for too long.
facts.def: To keep reading sad online news without stopping.

example.text: Stop doomscrolling and go to sleep.

misuse.text: Don't say 'doomscroll' about reading a recipe.

l1.hook: मध्यरात्रि, अभी भी बुरी ख़बरें "doomscroll" कर रहा हूँ!
l1.ex: "doomscroll" बंद करो और सो जाओ।

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: देर हो गया है, मैं सोने के लिए "catch some Zs" कर रहा हूँ!
l1.ex: मैं "catch some Zs" करने जा रहा हूँ।

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

l1.hook: एक झपकी, और मैं फिर से "good as new" हूँ!
l1.ex: एक झपकी के बाद, मैं "good as new" महसूस करता हूँ।

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

l1.hook: मीटिंग शुरू हो रही है, कौन "get the ball rolling" करेगा?
l1.ex: आइडियाज़ के साथ "get the ball rolling" शुरू करें।

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

l1.hook: क्या मैं तुम पर भरोसा कर सकता हूँ?
l1.ex: आज रात पिज़्ज़ा? "for sure"!

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

l1.hook: पार्टी आठ बजे खत्म हो गई। सच में?
l1.ex: वो पार्टी थोड़ी "lame" थी।

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

l1.hook: हम मुस्कुराते हैं, लेकिन प्रतिस्पर्धा करते हैं!
l1.ex: वह मेरी "frenemy" है, हमेशा मेरे साथ प्रतिस्पर्धा करती है।

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: वो कोट पुराने फिल्मों जैसा दिखता है!
l1.ex: वो कोट "it's giving" पुराने फिल्म सितारे जैसा है।

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: कठिन दिन रहा, लेकिन कल आ रहा है!
l1.ex: "chin up", कल बेहतर होगा।

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: डिनर तैयार है। कौन भूखा है? "dig in"
l1.ex: डिनर तैयार है, तो "dig in"!

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: चलना पड़ेगा। क्लास अभी शुरू हो रही है! "catch you later"
l1.ex: "catch you later", मुझे जाना है!

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: आखिरी सेकंड में गोल। हम जीत गए! "epic win"
l1.ex: हमने आखिरी सेकंड में गोल किया। "epic win"!

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

l1.hook: उस फिल्म के बारे में ईमानदार राय? "ngl"
l1.ex: "ngl", मुझे वह फिल्म बहुत पसंद आई।

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: केक गिर गया। सब देख रहे थे! "epic fail"
l1.ex: केक फट गया। पूरी तरह "epic fail"!

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

l1.hook: उपहार के लिए? कोई "chip in" करेगा?
l1.ex: चलो हम सब उसकी उपहार के लिए "chip in" करें।

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: कल टेस्ट है। हमें "game plan" कहाँ से शुरू करना चाहिए?
l1.ex: तो, game plan क्या है?

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

l1.hook: मेरे नए स्नीकर्स देखो! ये "fire" है।
l1.ex: वो स्नीकर्स fire हैं।

facts.def: A casual way to ask someone to repeat.

example.text: Come again? It's too loud here.

misuse.text: Don't say 'come again' when you heard clearly.

l1.hook: माफ़ करना, संगीत बहुत तेज़ है! क्या आप "come again" कह सकते हैं?
l1.ex: Come again? यहाँ बहुत तेज़ है।

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

l1.hook: अगले हफ़्ते फ़ाइनल्स हैं। पैनिक टाइम! अब हमें "hit the books" करना पड़ेगा।
l1.ex: मुझे आज रात hit the books करना है।

facts.def: People who love the same show or band.

example.text: The fandom loves this band.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers a 'fandom'.
misuse.why: It means devoted fans of one thing.

l1.hook: इस बैंड को सबसे ज़्यादा कौन पसंद करता है?
l1.ex: "fandom" इस बैंड को पसंद करता है।

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

l1.hook: वह ट्रेक अंतहीन जैसा लगा! मैं "dog tired" हूँ।
l1.ex: मैं "dog tired" हूँ, उस लंबी ट्रेक के बाद।

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: बाहर देखो! छाता ले लो! यह "raining cats and dogs" है।
l1.ex: यह "raining cats and dogs" है।

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

l1.hook: एक "heads up": बॉस आ रहा है।
l1.ex: बस "heads up", मीटिंग जल्दी शुरू होगी।

facts.def: Used when something doesn't seem logical.

example.text: This game rule makes no sense.

misuse.text: Don't say 'makes no sense' about your boss's plan.

l1.hook: नियम फिर से बदल गए। क्यों? "makes no sense"
l1.ex: इस खेल का नियम "makes no sense" है।

facts.def: Something unfair said to hurt someone.

example.text: That joke was a low blow.

misuse.text: Don't call fair criticism a 'low blow'.
misuse.why: It may just be honest feedback.

l1.hook: उसने उसकी पुरानी गलती का ज़िक्र किया! "low blow"
l1.ex: वह मज़ाक "low blow" था।

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: Pizza terbaik di kota. Percaya deh, "no cap".
l1.ex: Pizza ini yang terbaik di kota, no cap.

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: Dia kalah, lalu mengomel, "salty".
l1.ex: Dia "salty" karena aku menang dalam permainan kartu.

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: Kucing melompat ke dalam kotak! "I'm dead".
l1.ex: Kucing melompat ke dalam kotak. "I'm dead"!

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.hook: Seluruh pizza sudah habis! "pig out".
l1.ex: Kami "pig out" makan piza tadi malam.

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: Pizza jam enam, setuju? "bet".
l1.ex: Pizza jam enam? "bet".

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: Pizza dan film lagi? "basic".
l1.ex: Rencana akhir pekan saya "basic": pizza dan film.

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: Kedua orang itu berhenti berbicara. Kenapa? "beef".
l1.ex: Mereka punya "beef" karena sebuah permainan.

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: Kamarmu terlihat seperti Pinterest! "aesthetic".
l1.ex: Meja kamu terlihat sangat "aesthetic".

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.hook: Ayah melihat kamar berantakan! "blow a fuse".
l1.ex: Dia "blow a fuse" karena kamar yang berantakan.

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: Pasta buatan ibu terasa luar biasa malam ini! "bussin".
l1.ex: Pasta buatan ibu "bussin" malam ini.

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: Terima kasih banyak atas tumpangannya! "anytime".
l1.ex: Terima kasih atas tumpangannya! "anytime".

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: Lima menit, lalu aku kembali! "AFK".
l1.ex: Brb, saya akan "AFK" selama lima menit.

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: Di mana kunci itu pergi? "beats me".
l1.ex: Di mana kuncinya? "beats me".

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: Rencana gagal. Sekarang bagaimana? "back to square one".
l1.ex: Rencana gagal. "back to square one".

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: Lihat harga mantel ini! Itu 'arm and a leg'.
l1.ex: Mantel ini harganya "arm and a leg".

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: Oh, by the way!
l1.ex: By the way, pesta dimulai jam tujuh.

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: Kamu dapat tiket gratis untuk kami? Itu 'awesome'.
l1.ex: Kamu dapat tiket gratis untuk kami? Itu "awesome"!

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: Kucing mengantuk. Itu 'big mood'.
l1.ex: Kucing mengantuk itu "big mood".

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.hook: Hari ujian. Bagaimana hasilmu?
l1.ex: Aku 'ace' tes sejarahku hari ini!

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: Akhir pekan hujan. Seluruh musim. Ayo 'binge-watch'!
l1.ex: Aku akan "binge-watch" acara ini sepanjang akhir pekan.

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: Terlalu banyak kerja. Aku sudah 'burned out'!
l1.ex: Setelah ujian, aku merasa benar-benar 'burned out'.

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: Minggu lalu sakit, hari ini sudah 'back on my feet'!
l1.ex: Akhirnya aku sudah 'back on my feet'.

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: Aku butuh itu 'ASAP'!
l1.ex: Tolong kirim catatannya 'ASAP'.

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: Film malam ini jam enam, 'cool'?
l1.ex: 'Cool', sampai jumpa jam enam!

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: Dia tidak pernah bayar makan siang, 'cheap'!
l1.ex: Dia terlalu 'cheap' untuk membeli makan siang.

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.hook: Dia 'call out' kesalahanku ke semua orang!
l1.ex: Dia "call out" aku karena terlambat.

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.
