l1.hook: Hari wawancara. Aku 'dressed to impress' dengan setelan jas dan dasi!
l1.ex: Dia "dressed to impress" untuk wawancara.

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.hook: Dua jam slide yang sama! Aku 'bored stiff'.
l1.ex: Saya "bored stiff" di kelas itu.

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.hook: Sabtu. Diet? Diet apa? "cheat day"
l1.ex: Sabtu adalah "cheat day" saya.

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.hook: Siapa yang tahu semua rahasiamu, bestie?
l1.ex: "bestie" saya dan saya suka taco.

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.hook: Kamu lulus tes? Wow! "big W"
l1.ex: Kamu lulus tes? "big W"!

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.hook: Pizza nanas adalah yang terbaik! "hot take"
l1.ex: Ini "hot take"-ku: nanas pantas ada di pizza.

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: Dia tersandung dalam pertunjukan sekolah! "blooper"
l1.ex: "blooper" itu membuat seluruh kelas tertawa.

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.hook: Berapa kira-kiranya biayanya? "ballpark figure"
l1.ex: Berikan saya "ballpark figure".

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.hook: Malam permainan di rumahku! "count me in"
l1.ex: Malam permainan? "count me in"!

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.hook: Putar lagu ini lebih keras!
l1.ex: Lagu baru ini adalah "banger"!

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

l1.hook: Socks dengan sandal? Serius? big yikes
l1.ex: Kaos kaki dengan sandal? "big yikes".

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

l1.hook: Lampu panggung menyala. Otakku kosong! blank out
l1.ex: Saya "blank out" di tengah pidato saya.

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

l1.hook: Tiga jam video konyol! brain rot
l1.ex: Terlalu banyak video membuat saya "brain rot".

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

l1.hook: Tidak ada waktu luang minggu ini! busy as a bee
l1.ex: Saya "busy as a bee" minggu ini.

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

l1.hook: Di luar sangat dingin. Siap?
l1.ex: Bundle up, di luar sangat dingin!

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

l1.hook: Tidak ada waktu sekarang. Nanti?
l1.ex: Let's circle back ke situ setelah makan siang.

facts.def: Used to accept someone's point.

example.text: Fair enough, let's try your idea.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fair enough' to a rude insult.
misuse.why: It sounds like you agree with them.

l1.hook: Tunggu, dengarkan dulu alasan saya!
l1.ex: Fair enough, mari coba idemu.

facts.def: Describes things that are corny or too sweet.

example.text: That movie was so cheesy.

misuse.text: Don't call her poem 'cheesy' at the party.
misuse.why: It sounds mean about heartfelt effort.

l1.hook: Catatan cintanya berima. Ugh!
l1.ex: Film itu sangat cheesy.

facts.def: To answer criticism quickly and cleverly.

example.text: She clapped back with a great reply.

misuse.text: Don't 'clap back' at a parent's advice.

l1.hook: Dia mengejeknya. Dia membalas dengan "clap back"!
l1.ex: Dia "clap back" dengan balasan yang hebat.

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

l1.hook: Jaket baru, sepatu baru, percaya diri baru! "drip"
l1.ex: Jaketnya bagus, kamu punya "drip" hari ini.

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: Perjalanan dibatalkan. Semua orang "bummed out"!
l1.ex: Aku "bummed out" tentang perjalanan ini.

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

l1.hook: Coba ini dan beri tahu saya! "chef's kiss"
l1.ex: Supnya "chef's kiss".

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

l1.hook: Terima kasih sudah menyelamatkan PR-ku! "bro"
l1.ex: Terima kasih, "bro", kamu menyelamatkanku!

facts.def: To lead a team to victory with great skill.

example.text: Mia carried us in the final round.

misuse.text: Don't say 'she carried us' about a lazy teammate.
misuse.why: It praises someone who did the work.

l1.hook: Dia memenangkan pertandingan sendirian!
l1.ex: Mia "carry" kami di babak final.

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

l1.hook: Aku makan kuemu! Cuma bercanda ("just kidding").
l1.ex: Aku makan kuemu! Just kidding.

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

l1.hook: Aku lupa catatanku. Uh-oh!
l1.ex: Aku lupa catatanku. Aku "cooked".

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

l1.hook: Dia hanya minum teh mewah!
l1.ex: Kedai kopi ini sangat "bougie".

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

l1.hook: Mau pergi ke pertunjukan larut? "count me out".
l1.ex: Saya lelah, jadi "count me out".

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: Dia mengucapkan terima kasih kepada semua orang, bahkan kepada lawan!
l1.ex: Pelatih kami benar‑benar "class act".

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: Kamu lupa PR lagi?
l1.ex: "Bruh", kamu lupa PR lagi?

facts.def: To keep working late into the night.

example.text: We burned the midnight oil last night.

misuse.text: Don't say it about lighting candles.

l1.hook: Masih kerja sampai jam dua pagi?
l1.ex: Kami "burn the midnight oil" tadi malam.

facts.mean: A title that tricks you to click.
facts.def: A catchy headline that isn't worth reading.

example.text: That title is pure clickbait.

misuse.text: Don't call a real news story 'clickbait'.

l1.hook: "Kamu tidak akan percaya!" Sungguh?
l1.ex: Judul itu murni "clickbait".

facts.def: To decide to finish work or an activity for now.

example.text: We're tired, let's call it a day.

misuse.text: Don't 'call it a day' before the deadline.

l1.hook: Kami lelah. Lalu bagaimana?
l1.ex: Kami lelah, mari "call it a day".

facts.def: To begin to feel ill with something like a cold.

example.text: I think I'm coming down with a cold.

misuse.text: Don't say you 'came down with' a gift.
misuse.why: It means starting to get sick.

l1.hook: Tenggorokku sakit. Uh-oh! "come down with".
l1.ex: Kurasa aku sedang "come down with" flu.

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

l1.hook: Sedikit berita saja! "FYI".
l1.ex: FYI, toko tutup jam lima.

facts.def: Used to say you accept an idea.

example.text: Pizza or tacos? Fine by me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fine by me' when you're upset.
misuse.why: People will think you truly don't mind.

l1.hook: Pizza atau taco, pilih saja. "fine by me".
l1.ex: Pizza atau taco? Fine by me.

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

l1.hook: Lelucon ayah lagi. Serius? "corny".
l1.ex: Lelucon ayah sangat corny.

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.hook: Obrolan grup meledak karena hal sepele! "drama".
l1.ex: Aku nggak mau ada "drama" tahun ini.

facts.def: A moment to show your outfit and get opinions.

example.text: Quick fit check before school!

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'fit check' at the gym.

l1.hook: Pakaian siap. Pendapat sebelum sekolah? "fit check".
l1.ex: "Fit check" sebentar sebelum berangkat sekolah!

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.hook: Dia terlihat sedih. Lalu? "cheer up".
l1.ex: "Cheer up", kita mau makan pizza nih!

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.hook: Hari sedih? Sup hangat! "comfort food".
l1.ex: Sup hangat adalah "comfort food"-ku.

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: Siapa yang belajar bersamamu setiap malam? "buddy".
l1.ex: Dia itu teman belajar ("buddy") aku.

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.hook: Gol di detik terakhir yang "clutch" membuatnya menang!
l1.ex: Gol menit terakhir itu sangat "clutch".

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: Apakah toko ini "legit"?
l1.ex: Toko ini "legit", kakakku membeli sepatu di sana.

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

l1.hook: Aku baru, jadi "cut me some slack" ya.
l1.ex: "Cut me some slack", aku baru.

facts.def: To cost so much that you can't afford it.

example.text: Don't worry, this lunch won't break the bank.

misuse.text: Don't say 'break the bank' at a bank.
misuse.why: It only means costing too much.

l1.hook: Apakah makan siang ini akan "break the bank"?
l1.ex: Jangan khawatir, makan siang ini tidak akan "break the bank".

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: Silakan "drop by" kapan saja minggu ini!
l1.ex: Jangan ragu "drop by" kapan saja.

facts.def: Used when someone is doing really well at something.

example.text: You're crushing it at your new job!

misuse.text: Don't tell a struggling friend 'crushing it' sarcastically.

l1.hook: Minggu pertama, sudah jadi penjual teratas! "crushing it"
l1.ex: Kamu "crushing it" di pekerjaan barumu!

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: Perjalanan dibatalkan. Aduh! "bummer"
l1.ex: Perjalanan dibatalkan? Sungguh "bummer".

facts.def: To study many things quickly just before a test.

example.text: I must cram for math.

misuse.text: Don't 'cram' for a three-year course.
misuse.why: Cramming only works for short tests.

l1.hook: Ujian besok. Aku belum belajar! "cram"
l1.ex: Aku harus "cram" untuk matematika.

facts.mean: Scroll bad news for too long.
facts.def: To keep reading sad online news without stopping.

example.text: Stop doomscrolling and go to sleep.

misuse.text: Don't say 'doomscroll' about reading a recipe.

l1.hook: Tengah malam. Masih menggulir berita buruk! "doomscroll"
l1.ex: Berhenti "doomscroll" dan pergi tidur.

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: Sudah larut dan aku mengantuk! "catch some Zs"
l1.ex: Aku akan "catch some Zs".

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

l1.hook: Tidur sebentar, dan aku sudah "good as new"!
l1.ex: Setelah tidur sebentar, aku merasa "good as new".

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

l1.hook: Pertemuan dimulai. Siapa yang duluan? "Get the ball rolling".
l1.ex: Mari "get the ball rolling" dengan ide-ide.

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

l1.hook: Bolehkah aku mengandalkanmu? "For sure".
l1.ex: Pizza malam ini? "For sure"!

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

l1.hook: Pesta selesai jam delapan. Serius? "Lame".
l1.ex: Pesta itu agak "lame".

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

l1.hook: Kita tersenyum, tapi bersaing! "Frenemy".
l1.ex: Dia adalah "frenemy" ku, selalu bersaing denganku.

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: Mantel itu 'it's giving' nuansa film lama!
l1.ex: Mantel itu 'it's giving' vibe bintang film lama.

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: Hari yang berat, tapi besok akan datang. 'chin up'!
l1.ex: 'chin up', besok akan lebih baik.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: Makan malam sudah siap. Siapa yang lapar? 'dig in'!
l1.ex: Makan malam sudah siap, jadi 'dig in'!

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: Aku harus pergi. Kelas mulai sekarang! 'catch you later'!
l1.ex: 'catch you later', aku harus pergi!

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: Gol di detik terakhir. Kita menang! 'epic win'!
l1.ex: Kami mencetak gol di detik terakhir. 'epic win'!

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

l1.hook: Pendapat jujur tentang film itu? "ngl"
l1.ex: Ngl, aku suka film itu.

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: Kueku runtuh. Semua orang menonton! "epic fail"
l1.ex: Kuenya datar. Total epic fail!

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

l1.hook: Hadiah untuk dia? Ada yang mau "chip in"?
l1.ex: Ayo semua chip in untuk hadiah dia.

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: Ujian besok. Dari mana kita mulai? "game plan"
l1.ex: Jadi, apa game plan-nya?

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

l1.hook: Lihat sepatu baru ku! "fire"
l1.ex: Sepatu itu fire!

facts.def: A casual way to ask someone to repeat.

example.text: Come again? It's too loud here.

misuse.text: Don't say 'come again' when you heard clearly.

l1.hook: Maaf, musiknya terlalu keras!
l1.ex: "Come again"? Di sini terlalu berisik.

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

l1.hook: Ujian akhir minggu depan. Saatnya panik!
l1.ex: Saya harus "hit the books" malam ini.

facts.def: People who love the same show or band.

example.text: The fandom loves this band.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers a 'fandom'.
misuse.why: It means devoted fans of one thing.

l1.hook: Siapa yang paling menyukai band ini?
l1.ex: The fandom menyukai band ini.

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

l1.hook: Pendakian itu terasa tak berujung!
l1.ex: Saya "dog tired" setelah pendakian panjang itu.

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: Lihat ke luar! Ambil payung!
l1.ex: "It's raining cats and dogs"!

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

l1.hook: "heads up", bos datang!
l1.ex: Sekadar "heads up", rapat dimulai lebih awal.

facts.def: Used when something doesn't seem logical.

example.text: This game rule makes no sense.

misuse.text: Don't say 'makes no sense' about your boss's plan.

l1.hook: "makes no sense" - aturan berubah lagi. Kenapa?
l1.ex: Aturan permainan ini "makes no sense".

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: この街で一番のピザだよ。信じてね、"no cap"
l1.ex: このピザはこの街で一番だ、"no cap"。

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: 彼は負けてからすねた、"salty"。
l1.ex: カードゲームで勝ったから、彼は"salty"だ。

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: 猫が箱に飛び込んだ！"I'm dead"
l1.ex: 猫が箱に飛び込んだ。"I'm dead!"

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.hook: ピザが全部なくなった！"pig out"
l1.ex: 昨晩、ピザで"pig out"した。

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: 6時にピザ、どう？"bet"
l1.ex: 6時にピザ？"Bet"。

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: またピザと映画か？
l1.ex: 私の週末の予定は「basic」だ：ピザと映画。

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: あの二人は話さなくなった。どうして？
l1.ex: 彼らはゲームのことで「beef」している。

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: 君の部屋、Pinterestみたいだね！
l1.ex: 君のデスクはとても「aesthetic」だね。

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.hook: パパが散らかった部屋を見たんだ！
l1.ex: 彼は散らかった部屋のことで「blow a fuse」した。

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: ママのパスタ、今夜はとても美味しいね！
l1.ex: ママのパスタは今夜「bussin」だね。

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: 乗せてくれて本当にありがとう！「anytime」
l1.ex: 乗せてくれてありがとう！anytime

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: 5分だけ離れるね、すぐに戻るよ。「AFK」
l1.ex: すぐ戻るね、5分間AFKになるよ。

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: 鍵がどこに行ったのか分からない。「beats me」
l1.ex: 鍵はどこ？Beats me。

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: 計画が失敗した。次はどうしよう？「back to square one」
l1.ex: 計画が失敗した。Back to square one。

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: このコートの値段を見て！「arm and a leg」
l1.ex: このコートは arm and a leg だ。

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: あ、もうひとつだけ、by the way。
l1.ex: by the way、パーティーは7時に始まるよ。

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: 無料チケットを手に入れたんだね？「awesome」
l1.ex: 無料チケットを手に入れたんだ？それはawesome！

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: 眠そうな猫。big moodだね。
l1.ex: あの眠そうな猫はbig moodだ。

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.hook: テストの日だね。結果はどうだった？「ace」
l1.ex: 今日、歴史のテストをaceしたよ！

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: 雨の週末。シーズン全体をbinge-watchしよう！
l1.ex: 週末ずっとこの番組をbinge-watchするよ。

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: 仕事が多すぎて、もう"burned out"だ！
l1.ex: 試験が終わって、完全に"burned out"だった。

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: 先週は病気だったけど、今日は"back on my feet"だ！
l1.ex: やっと"back on my feet"になった。

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: 今すぐ欲しい、つまり"ASAP"だ！
l1.ex: ノートを"ASAP"で送ってください。

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: 今夜6時に映画、いい？"cool"
l1.ex: "cool"、6時に会いましょう！

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: 彼は昼食代を絶対に払わない。"cheap"
l1.ex: 彼は昼食を買うほど「cheap」だ。

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.hook: 彼女はみんなに僕のミスを指摘した。「call out」
l1.ex: 彼女は私が遅れたことを「call out」した。

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.hook: 面接の日。スーツにネクタイ！『dressed to impress』
l1.ex: 彼は面接のために「dressed to impress」な服装だ。

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.hook: 同じスライドが2時間！『bored stiff』
l1.ex: あの授業で私は「bored stiff」だった。

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.hook: 土曜日。ダイエット？どんなダイエット？『cheat day』
l1.ex: 土曜日は私の「cheat day」だ。

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.hook: 誰があなたのすべての秘密を知っているの？『bestie』
l1.ex: 私の「bestie」と私はタコスが大好きだ。

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.hook: テストに合格したの？big W！
l1.ex: テストに合格したの？Big W！

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.hook: パイナップルピザが最高だ！『hot take』
l1.ex: これが私のhot takeです：パイナップルはピザに合うべきだ。

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: 彼は学園劇でつまずいた！『blooper』
l1.ex: そのblooperでクラス全員が笑った。

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.hook: いくらかかりますか？『ballpark figure』
l1.ex: ballpark figureを教えて。

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.hook: 私の家でゲームナイト！『count me in』
l1.ex: ゲームナイト？Count me in！

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.hook: この曲をもっと大音量で流して！『banger』
l1.ex: この新しい曲は "banger" です！

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

l1.hook: サンダルに靴下？本当に？『big yikes』
l1.ex: サンダルに靴下？ "big yikes"

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

l1.hook: ステージのライトがついた。頭が「blank out」した。
l1.ex: スピーチの途中で "blank out" した。

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

l1.m: 脳みそが腐るようなコンテンツ
l1.hook: ３時間も "brain rot" な動画を見た！
l1.ex: 動画を見過ぎると "brain rot" になる。

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

l1.hook: 今週は "busy as a bee" で、自由な時間がない！
l1.ex: 今週は "busy as a bee" です。

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

l1.hook: 外は凍えるほど寒いよ。'bundle up'する準備はできた？
l1.ex: 「Bundle up」、外は凍えるほど寒いよ！

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

l1.hook: 今は時間がないな。あとでまた「circle back」（折り返し連絡／戻って議論）する？
l1.ex: 昼食の後で「circle back」しよう。

facts.def: Used to accept someone's point.

example.text: Fair enough, let's try your idea.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fair enough' to a rude insult.
misuse.why: It sounds like you agree with them.

l1.hook: 待って、まず私の理由を聞いて！ 「fair enough」がぴったりの場面です。
l1.ex: 「Fair enough」、君のアイデアを試してみよう。

facts.def: Describes things that are corny or too sweet.

example.text: That movie was so cheesy.

misuse.text: Don't call her poem 'cheesy' at the party.
misuse.why: It sounds mean about heartfelt effort.

l1.hook: 彼のラブレター、韻を踏んでるよ。うわぁ…！ 「cheesy」ってどういう意味？
l1.ex: あの映画はとても「cheesy」だった。

facts.def: To answer criticism quickly and cleverly.

example.text: She clapped back with a great reply.

misuse.text: Don't 'clap back' at a parent's advice.

l1.hook: 彼が彼女をからかったら、彼女が言い返した！ 「clap back」をチェック。
l1.ex: 彼女は「clap back」して、素晴らしい返答をした。

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

l1.hook: 新しいジャケットに新しい靴、そして新しい自信！'drip'だね。
l1.ex: いいジャケットだね、今日は「drip」だね。

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: 旅行が中止。みんなガッカリ… 「bummed out」を使ってみよう。
l1.ex: 旅行のことがあって、僕は「bummed out」だ。

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

l1.hook: これ食べて感想教えて！ まさに「chef's kiss」な瞬間です。
l1.ex: そのスープは「chef's kiss」だった。

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

l1.hook: 宿題助けてくれてありがとな！ 「bro」の使い方をマスターしよう。
l1.ex: ありがとう、bro、助かったよ！

facts.def: To lead a team to victory with great skill.

example.text: Mia carried us in the final round.

misuse.text: Don't say 'she carried us' about a lazy teammate.
misuse.why: It praises someone who did the work.

l1.hook: 彼女が単独で試合を勝利に導いた！ 「carry」の意味を知っていますか？
l1.ex: Miaは決勝ラウンドで私たちを「carry」した。

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

l1.hook: あなたのケーキを食べちゃった！（just kidding）
l1.ex: あなたのケーキを食べたよ。just kidding。

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

l1.hook: ノートを忘れちゃった。うわっ！（cooked）
l1.ex: ノートを忘れた。I'm cooked。

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

l1.hook: 彼女は高級な紅茶しか飲まない！（bougie）
l1.ex: このコーヒーショップはとてもbougieです。

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

l1.hook: 深夜ショーに行きたい？（count me out）
l1.ex: 疲れたから、count me out。

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: 彼はライバルさえもみんなに感謝した！（class act）
l1.ex: 私たちのコーチは本当にclass actだ。

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: "bruh"、また宿題を忘れたの？
l1.ex: "Bruh"、また宿題を忘れたの？

facts.def: To keep working late into the night.

example.text: We burned the midnight oil last night.

misuse.text: Don't say it about lighting candles.

l1.hook: まだ午前2時に仕事してるの？'burn the midnight oil'してるね。
l1.ex: 私たちは昨晩「burn the midnight oil」した。

facts.mean: A title that tricks you to click.
facts.def: A catchy headline that isn't worth reading.

example.text: That title is pure clickbait.

misuse.text: Don't call a real news story 'clickbait'.

l1.hook: 『信じられない！』って本当？'clickbait'だね。
l1.ex: あのタイトルは純粋に "clickbait" だ。

facts.def: To decide to finish work or an activity for now.

example.text: We're tired, let's call it a day.

misuse.text: Don't 'call it a day' before the deadline.

l1.m: 今日はここまでにする
l1.hook: みんな疲れたね。どうする？'call it a day'しようか。
l1.ex: 疲れたから "call it a day" しよう。

facts.def: To begin to feel ill with something like a cold.

example.text: I think I'm coming down with a cold.

misuse.text: Don't say you 'came down with' a gift.
misuse.why: It means starting to get sick.

l1.hook: 喉が痛いんだ。うわっ！'come down with'かもしれないね。
l1.ex: 風邪を「come down with」かもしれない。

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

l1.hook: FYI、ちょっとしたニュースです！
l1.ex: FYI、店は5時に閉まります。

facts.def: Used to say you accept an idea.

example.text: Pizza or tacos? Fine by me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fine by me' when you're upset.
misuse.why: People will think you truly don't mind.

l1.hook: ピザかタコス、どっちがいい？
l1.ex: ピザかタコス？ Fine by me。

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

l1.hook: また父のダジャレか。マジで？
l1.ex: 父のジョークはすごく corny。

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.hook: グループチャットが何でもないことで大騒ぎした！
l1.ex: 今年は drama は要らない。

facts.def: A moment to show your outfit and get opinions.

example.text: Quick fit check before school!

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'fit check' at the gym.

l1.hook: 服装は準備できた。学校に行く前に感想は？
l1.ex: 学校に行く前に quick fit check！

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.hook: 彼女が悲しそうだね。どうする？'cheer up'しよう。
l1.ex: "cheer up"、ピザを食べるよ！

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.hook: つらい日？温かいスープが'comfort food'だね。
l1.ex: 温かいスープは私の "comfort food" です。

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: 毎晩一緒に勉強してくれるのは誰？'buddy'は誰？
l1.ex: 彼は私の勉強 "buddy" です。

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.hook: 最後の秒で決めたゴールが勝負を決めた！'clutch'だね。
l1.ex: あの最後のゴールはとても "clutch" だった。

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: この店は legit ですか？
l1.ex: この店は "legit" です、妹がそこで靴を買いました。

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

l1.hook: 私、初心者です。"cut me some slack"、優しくお願いします！
l1.ex: 「Cut me some slack」、私は初心者です。

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: 今週はいつでも drop by してね。
l1.ex: いつでも「drop by」してください。

facts.def: Used when someone is doing really well at something.

example.text: You're crushing it at your new job!

misuse.text: Don't tell a struggling friend 'crushing it' sarcastically.

l1.hook: 最初の週なのに、すでに crushing it です！
l1.ex: あなたは新しい仕事で「crushing it」だね。

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: 旅行がキャンセルになってしまった。bummer だね。
l1.ex: 旅行がキャンセル？なんて「bummer」だ。

facts.def: To study many things quickly just before a test.

example.text: I must cram for math.

misuse.text: Don't 'cram' for a three-year course.
misuse.why: Cramming only works for short tests.

l1.hook: 明日試験なのに、まだ cram していない！
l1.ex: 数学のために "cram" しなきゃ。

facts.mean: Scroll bad news for too long.
facts.def: To keep reading sad online news without stopping.

example.text: Stop doomscrolling and go to sleep.

misuse.text: Don't say 'doomscroll' about reading a recipe.

l1.m: ドゥームスクロールする
l1.hook: 真夜中に、まだ doomscroll している。
l1.ex: 「doomscroll」するのをやめて、寝よう。

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: 遅くなって眠いから、catch some Zs しよう。
l1.ex: 「catch some Zs」しよう。

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

l1.hook: ひと眠りしたら、good as new だ。
l1.ex: 昼寝の後、私は "good as new" だ。

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

l1.hook: ミーティングが始まります。誰が最初に「get the ball rolling」しますか？
l1.ex: アイデアで "get the ball rolling" しよう。

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

l1.hook: 「Can I count on you?」と聞かれたら、"for sure" と答えてみよう。
l1.ex: 「Pizza tonight?」と聞かれたら、"for sure" と答える。

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

l1.hook: 「Party ended at eight. Seriously?」と聞かれたら、"lame" と言ってみよう。
l1.ex: あのパーティーはちょっと "lame" だった。

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

l1.hook: 「We smile, but we compete!」と聞かれたら、"frenemy" と言ってみよう。
l1.ex: 彼女は私の "frenemy" で、いつも私と競い合っている。

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: 「That coat looks like old movies!」と聞かれたら、"it's giving" と言ってみよう。
l1.ex: あのコートは "it's giving" old movie star のようだ。

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: 「Rough day, but tomorrow's coming!」と聞かれたら、"chin up" と言ってみよう。
l1.ex: "chin up"、明日はもっと良くなるよ。

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: ディナーができました。誰が「dig in」しますか？
l1.ex: ディナーができたよ、"dig in"！

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: 行かなきゃ。授業が始まるから、"catch you later"
l1.ex: "catch you later"、行かなきゃ！

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: 最後の秒でゴール！勝ったよ、"epic win"
l1.ex: 最後の秒で得点したよ。"epic win"

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: ケーキが崩れた。みんな見てたよ、"epic fail"
l1.ex: ケーキが失敗した。完全に「epic fail」だ！

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

l1.hook: 彼女へのプレゼント？誰か『chip in』？」
l1.ex: みんなで"chip in"して彼女へのプレゼントを出そう。

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: 明日テストです。どこから始めるか、"game plan" を決めましょうか？
l1.ex: で、何が"game plan"？

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

l1.hook: 新しいスニーカーを見て！めっちゃ「fire」！
l1.ex: あのスニーカーは"fire"だ！

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

l1.hook: 来週は期末試験だ。慌てて「hit the books」しなきゃ！
l1.ex: 今夜は"hit the books"しなきゃ。

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: 外を見て！傘を持って！ "raining cats and dogs" です。
l1.ex: 今、"raining cats and dogs" です！

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

l1.hook: heads up、上司が来ます！
l1.ex: heads up、会議は早く始まります。

facts.def: Used when something doesn't seem logical.

example.text: This game rule makes no sense.

misuse.text: Don't say 'makes no sense' about your boss's plan.

l1.hook: ルールがまた変わった。なぜ？「makes no sense」
l1.ex: このゲームのルールは "makes no sense" です。

facts.def: Something unfair said to hurt someone.

example.text: That joke was a low blow.

misuse.text: Don't call fair criticism a 'low blow'.
misuse.why: It may just be honest feedback.

l1.hook: 彼は彼女の昔のミスを言及した！「low blow」
l1.ex: あのジョークは「low blow」だった。

facts.mean: Succeed at wearing or doing something bold.
facts.def: To manage something hard or bold, like a style.

example.text: Not everyone can pull off that color.

misuse.text: Don't say 'pull off' when you mean 'remove'.

l1.hook: 他に誰がそれを「pull off」できるかな？
l1.ex: 誰でもその色を「pull off」できるわけではない。

facts.mean: Grumpy and in a bad mood.
facts.def: Describes someone tired or annoyed.

example.text: I'm cranky before breakfast.

misuse.text: Don't call your boss 'cranky' in an email.

l1.hook: まだ私に話しかけないで、「cranky」だ。
l1.ex: 朝食前は「cranky」だ。

facts.mean: A person who loves good food.
facts.def: Someone who enjoys trying and talking about food.
facts.hook: She reviews every restaurant in town!

example.text: My sister is a total foodie.

misuse.text: Don't call a chef a 'foodie'.
misuse.why: A chef cooks; a foodie loves eating.

l1.hook: 彼女は街のすべてのレストランをレビューする「foodie」だ。
l1.ex: 私の妹は完全な「foodie」だ。

facts.def: A British way to say thank you or goodbye.
facts.hook: He held the door. Say thanks!

example.text: Cheers for the lift!

misuse.text: Don't expect Americans to understand 'cheers' as thanks.

l1.hook: 彼がドアを開けてくれた。'cheers' と言って感謝しよう。
l1.ex: 'cheers'、乗せてくれてありがとう！

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: 이 동네 최고의 피자야. 믿어, no cap
l1.ex: 이 피자는 이 동네에서 최고야, no cap

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: 그는 졌고, 화가 났다! "salty"
l1.ex: 그는 내가 카드 게임에서 이겨서 'salty'했어.

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: 고양이가 상자 안으로 뛰어들었어! I'm dead
l1.ex: 고양이가 상자 안으로 뛰어들었어. I'm dead!

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.hook: 피자 전체가 다 사라졌어! pig out
l1.ex: 우리는 어젯밤 피자를 많이 먹었어. "pig out"

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: 6시에 피자 어때, bet?
l1.ex: 6시에 피자? Bet

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: 피자와 영화를 또? 'basic'이야.
l1.ex: 내 주말 계획은 basic: 피자와 영화야.

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: 그 두 사람은 말을 끊었어. 왜? 'beef'?
l1.ex: 그들은 게임 때문에 beef가 있어.

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: 네 방이 Pinterest처럼 보여! 'aesthetic'!
l1.ex: 네 책상이 정말 aesthetic해.

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.hook: 아빠가 지저분한 방을 보시고 'blow a fuse'했어.
l1.ex: 그는 어질러진 방 때문에 blow a fuse했어.

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: 엄마의 파스타가 오늘 밤에 정말 'bussin'해!
l1.ex: 엄마 파스타가 오늘 밤에 bussin이야.

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: 태워줘서 정말 고마워! "anytime".
l1.ex: 태워줘서 고마워! "anytime".

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: 5분 뒤에 돌아올게! 'AFK'
l1.ex: 잠깐 나갔다 올게, 5분 동안 "AFK" 할게.

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: 열쇠가 어디로 갔지? 'beats me'
l1.ex: 열쇠가 어디 있지? "beats me".

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: 계획이 실패했어. 이제 "back to square one"이야.
l1.ex: 계획이 실패했어. "back to square one".

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: 이 코트 가격을 봐! "arm and a leg"이야.
l1.ex: 이 코트는 "arm and a leg" 정도야.

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: by the way, 아, 한 가지 더!
l1.ex: by the way, 파티는 7시에 시작해.

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: 우리에게 무료 티켓을 구했어? "awesome"!
l1.ex: 우리에게 무료 티켓을 구했어? "awesome"!

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: 잠자는 고양이. 바로 내 기분! "big mood"
l1.ex: 그 잠자는 고양이는 "big mood".

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.hook: 시험 날이야. 어떻게 했어? "ace"!
l1.ex: 오늘 역사 시험을 "ace"했어!

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: 비 오는 주말이야. 시즌 전체를 "binge-watch"하자!
l1.ex: 주말 내내 이 쇼를 "binge-watch" 할 거야.

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: 일이 너무 많아. 나 이제 'burned out'이야.
l1.ex: 시험이 끝난 뒤, 나는 완전히 'burned out'했어.

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: 지난주에 아팠지만, 오늘은 괜찮아. 이제 'back on my feet'야.
l1.ex: 드디어 'back on my feet'야.

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: 지금 바로 필요해! 'ASAP'.
l1.ex: 노트를 'ASAP'로 보내 주세요.

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: 오늘 밤 6시에 영화 보자, 괜찮아? 'cool'.
l1.ex: 'Cool', 6시에 보자!

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: 그는 점심값을 절대 안 내, 'cheap'.
l1.ex: 그는 점심을 사기엔 너무 'cheap'해.

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.hook: 그녀는 모두에게 내 실수를 'call out'했어.
l1.ex: 그녀는 내가 늦은 것을 'call out'했어.

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.hook: 면접 날. 정장과 넥타이, 'dressed to impress'!
l1.ex: 그는 면접을 위해 'dressed to impress'하게 옷을 입었어.

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.hook: 같은 슬라이드 두 시간! 'bored stiff'!
l1.ex: 그 수업에서 나는 'bored stiff'했어.

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.hook: 토요일. 다이어트? 무슨 다이어트? 'cheat day'!
l1.ex: 토요일은 나의 'cheat day'야.

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.hook: 누가 네 모든 비밀을 알까? 'bestie'!
l1.ex: 내 'bestie'와 나는 타코를 좋아해.

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.hook: 시험에 합격했어? 와, "big W"!
l1.ex: 시험에 합격했어? "big W"!

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.hook: "hot take" 파인애플 피자가 최고야!
l1.ex: 내 "hot take": 파인애플은 피자에 들어가야 해.

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: 그는 학교 연극에서 넘어졌어! "blooper"
l1.ex: 그 "blooper" 때문에 반 전체가 웃었어.

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.hook: 얼마 정도 들까? "ballpark figure"
l1.ex: "ballpark figure" 알려줘.

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.hook: 우리 집에서 게임 나이트 할 거야! "count me in"
l1.ex: 게임 나이트? "count me in"!

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.hook: 이 노래를 더 크게 틀어! "banger"!
l1.ex: 이 새 노래는 "banger"야!

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

l1.hook: 샌들에 양말? 정말? "big yikes"!
l1.ex: 샌들에 양말? "big yikes".

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

l1.hook: 무대 조명이 켜졌다. 내 머릿속이 텅 비었다! "blank out"
l1.ex: 연설 중에 나는 "blank out" 했어.

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

l1.hook: 'brain rot' 같은 어리석은 영상을 세 시간이나 봤어!
l1.ex: 영상이 너무 많으면 나는 "brain rot"이 돼.

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

l1.hook: 이번 주는 자유 시간이 없어! "busy as a bee"
l1.ex: 이번 주에 나는 "busy as a bee"야.

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

l1.hook: 밖이 너무 추워. "bundle up" 할 준비됐어?
l1.ex: 따뜻하게 입어('Bundle up'), 밖이 엄청 추워!

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

l1.hook: 지금은 시간이 없어. "circle back" 할래?
l1.ex: 점심 먹고 나서 그 문제로 다시 돌아오죠('circle back').

facts.def: Used to accept someone's point.

example.text: Fair enough, let's try your idea.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fair enough' to a rude insult.
misuse.why: It sounds like you agree with them.

l1.hook: 잠깐, 내 이유부터 들어봐! "fair enough"?
l1.ex: 좋아, 일리 있네('Fair enough'). 네 아이디어대로 해보자.

facts.def: Describes things that are corny or too sweet.

example.text: That movie was so cheesy.

misuse.text: Don't call her poem 'cheesy' at the party.
misuse.why: It sounds mean about heartfelt effort.

l1.hook: 그의 연애 편지가 운율 맞게 적혔어. 으악! "cheesy".
l1.ex: 그 영화는 너무 유치하고 오글거렸어('cheesy').

facts.def: To answer criticism quickly and cleverly.

example.text: She clapped back with a great reply.

misuse.text: Don't 'clap back' at a parent's advice.

l1.hook: 그가 그녀를 비웃었어. 그녀가 "clap back" 했어!
l1.ex: 그녀는 멋진 답글로 통쾌하게 맞받아쳤어('clapped back').

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

l1.hook: 새 재킷, 새 신발, 새 자신감! "drip".
l1.ex: 멋진 재킷이네, 오늘 'drip' 좀 있는데.

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: 여행이 취소됐어. 모두 "bummed out" 했어.
l1.ex: 나 이번 여행 취소되어서 완전히 'bummed out' 상태야.

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

l1.hook: 이거 맛보고 말해줘! "chef's kiss".
l1.ex: 그 수프는 정말 'chef's kiss'였어.

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

l1.hook: 숙제 구해줘서 고마워, bro!
l1.ex: 고마워, 'bro', 네가 날 살렸어!

facts.def: To lead a team to victory with great skill.

example.text: Mia carried us in the final round.

misuse.text: Don't say 'she carried us' about a lazy teammate.
misuse.why: It praises someone who did the work.

l1.hook: 그녀가 혼자서 경기에서 이겼어! "carry".
l1.ex: 미아가 결승전에서 우리 팀을 'carry'했어.

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

l1.hook: "just kidding" 네 케이크를 먹었어!
l1.ex: 나 네 케이크 먹었어! "Just kidding."

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

l1.hook: 나 노트 두고 왔어. 어쩌지!
l1.ex: 나 노트 두고 왔어. I'm "cooked".

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

l1.hook: 얘는 고급 차만 마셔!
l1.ex: 이 카페 진짜 너무 "bougie"하다.

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

l1.hook: 심야 영화 보러 갈래?
l1.ex: 나 피곤하니까 "count me out".

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: 그 사람은 라이벌한테도 감사 인사를 전했어!
l1.ex: 우리 감독님은 정말 "class act"야.

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: "bruh" 숙제를 또 잊었어?
l1.ex: "Bruh", 너 숙제 또 까먹었어?

facts.def: To keep working late into the night.

example.text: We burned the midnight oil last night.

misuse.text: Don't say it about lighting candles.

l1.hook: "burn the midnight oil" 새벽 2시에 아직도 일하고 있어?
l1.ex: 우리는 어젯밤에 "burn the midnight oil" 했어.

facts.mean: A title that tricks you to click.
facts.def: A catchy headline that isn't worth reading.

example.text: That title is pure clickbait.

misuse.text: Don't call a real news story 'clickbait'.

l1.hook: "clickbait" '믿을 수 없을 거야!' 정말?
l1.ex: 저 제목은 완전 "clickbait"야.

facts.def: To decide to finish work or an activity for now.

example.text: We're tired, let's call it a day.

misuse.text: Don't 'call it a day' before the deadline.

l1.hook: "call it a day" 우리는 피곤해. 이제 뭐 할까?
l1.ex: 우리 피곤한데, 이만 "call it a day" 하자.

facts.def: To begin to feel ill with something like a cold.

example.text: I think I'm coming down with a cold.

misuse.text: Don't say you 'came down with' a gift.
misuse.why: It means starting to get sick.

l1.hook: "come down with" 목이 아파. 어쩌지?
l1.ex: 나 감기에 "come down with" 하는 것 같아.

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

l1.hook: "fyi" 작은 소식이야!
l1.ex: FYI, 그 가게는 5시에 문을 닫아.

facts.def: Used to say you accept an idea.

example.text: Pizza or tacos? Fine by me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fine by me' when you're upset.
misuse.why: People will think you truly don't mind.

l1.hook: "fine by me" 피자든 타코든 네가 골라!
l1.ex: 피자 아니면 타코? Fine by me.

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

l1.hook: "corny" 아빠가 또 말장난이야. 진심이야?
l1.ex: 우리 아빠 농담은 너무 corny해.

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.hook: "drama" 그룹 채팅이 별일도 아닌데 폭발했어!
l1.ex: 올해는 어떤 drama도 겪고 싶지 않아.

facts.def: A moment to show your outfit and get opinions.

example.text: Quick fit check before school!

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'fit check' at the gym.

l1.hook: ‘fit check’ 준비됐어. 학교 가기 전에 생각 있어?
l1.ex: 등교 전에 빠르게 fit check!

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.hook: 그녀가 슬퍼 보여요. 이제 어떻게 하죠?
l1.ex: "Cheer up", 우리 피자 먹을 거잖아!

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.hook: 슬픈 날인가요? 따뜻한 수프!
l1.ex: 따뜻한 수프는 나의 "comfort food"예요.

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: 매일 밤 당신과 함께 공부하는 사람은 누구인가요?
l1.ex: 그는 제 스터디 "buddy"예요.

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.hook: 마지막 1초 전 골로 승리했습니다!
l1.ex: 그 마지막 1분 전 골은 정말 "clutch"했어요.

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: 이 가게 진짜인가요?
l1.ex: 이 가게는 "legit"해요, 제 언니도 거기서 신발을 샀거든요.

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

l1.hook: ‘cut me some slack’, 난 처음이야. 부디 좀 봐줘!
l1.ex: 나 신입이야, 'cut me some slack'(봐주면서 해줘).

facts.def: To cost so much that you can't afford it.

example.text: Don't worry, this lunch won't break the bank.

misuse.text: Don't say 'break the bank' at a bank.
misuse.why: It only means costing too much.

l1.hook: ‘break the bank’ 할 정도로 점심값이 비싸?
l1.ex: 걱정 마, 이 점심은 'break the bank'(큰돈이 들다) 하지 않을 거야.

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: ‘drop by’ 이번 주 언제든 와도 돼!
l1.ex: 언제든 편하게 'drop by'(잠깐 들르다) 하세요.

facts.def: Used when someone is doing really well at something.

example.text: You're crushing it at your new job!

misuse.text: Don't tell a struggling friend 'crushing it' sarcastically.

l1.hook: ‘crushing it’, 첫 주에 이미 최고 판매자야!
l1.ex: 새 직장에서 정말 'crushing it'(엄청 잘하다) 하고 있구나!

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: ‘bummer’, 여행이 취소됐어. 아쉽다!
l1.ex: 여행이 취소됐다고? 정말 'bummer'(아쉬운 일)네.

facts.def: To study many things quickly just before a test.

example.text: I must cram for math.

misuse.text: Don't 'cram' for a three-year course.
misuse.why: Cramming only works for short tests.

l1.hook: ‘cram’, 내일 시험인데 아직 공부를 못 했어!
l1.ex: 수학을 위해 'cram' 해야 해.

facts.mean: Scroll bad news for too long.
facts.def: To keep reading sad online news without stopping.

example.text: Stop doomscrolling and go to sleep.

misuse.text: Don't say 'doomscroll' about reading a recipe.

l1.hook: ‘doomscroll’, 새벽이야. 아직도 나쁜 소식만 스크롤하고 있어!
l1.ex: 'doomscroll'을 멈추고 잠자리에 들어.

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: ‘catch some Zs’, 늦었고 졸려!
l1.ex: 'catch some Zs' 할게.

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

l1.hook: ‘good as new’, 한 번 낮잠 자면 완전히 회복돼!
l1.ex: 잠을 잔 뒤에 나는 'good as new' 느낌이야.

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

l1.hook: "get the ball rolling" 회의가 시작됩니다. 누가 먼저 할까요?
l1.ex: 'get the ball rolling' 하자.

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

l1.hook: 너에게 기대해도 돼? "for sure".
l1.ex: 피자 오늘 밤? "for sure"!

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

l1.hook: 파티가 8시에 끝났어. 진짜? 완전 'lame'이야.
l1.ex: 그 파티는 좀 "lame".

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

l1.hook: 우리는 웃지만 경쟁해! "frenemy"
l1.ex: 그녀는 내 "frenemy"이고, 항상 나와 경쟁해.

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: "it's giving" 그 코트는 옛날 영화 같아!
l1.ex: "it's giving" 그 코트는 옛날 영화 스타 느낌이야.

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: "chin up" 힘든 하루였지만 내일이 와!
l1.ex: 'Chin up', 내일은 더 나아질 거야.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: 저녁 준비됐어. 누가 배고프니?
l1.ex: 저녁이 준비됐으니 'dig in'!

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: 가야 해. 지금 수업이 시작돼!
l1.ex: 'catch you later', 나 가야 해!

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: 마지막 순간에 골이 들어갔어. 우리가 이겼어!
l1.ex: 마지막 순간에 득점했어. 'epic win'!

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

l1.hook: 그 영화에 대한 솔직한 의견이 뭐야?
l1.ex: 'ngl', 그 영화 정말 좋았어.

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: 내 케이크가 무너졌어. 모두가 봤어!
l1.ex: 내 케이크가 납작해졌어. 완전 'epic fail'이야!

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

l1.hook: 그녀에게 줄 선물? ‘chip in’ 할 사람?
l1.ex: 우리 모두 ‘chip in’ 해서 그녀 선물에 돈을 모으자.

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: 내일 시험이야. 어디서부터 ‘game plan’을 세워야 할까?
l1.ex: 그럼, ‘game plan’이 뭐야?

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

l1.hook: 내 새 스니커즈 좀 봐! 완전 ‘fire’!
l1.ex: 그 스니커즈 진짜 ‘fire’!

facts.def: A casual way to ask someone to repeat.

example.text: Come again? It's too loud here.

misuse.text: Don't say 'come again' when you heard clearly.

l1.hook: 미안, 음악이 너무 시끄러워! ‘come again’?
l1.ex: ‘come again’? 여기 너무 시끄러워.

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

l1.hook: 다음 주에 기말고사야. ‘hit the books’ 해야 할 시간!
l1.ex: 오늘 밤에 "hit the books" 해야 해.

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

l1.hook: 그 등산은 끝이 없는 것 같았어. 완전 'dog tired'했어.
l1.ex: 나는 그 긴 등산 후에 "dog tired"다.

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: 밖을 봐! 우산을 챙겨! 비가 'raining cats and dogs'처럼 억수로 와.
l1.ex: 지금 "raining cats and dogs"이야!

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

l1.hook: 잠깐 "heads up": 사장이 온다!
l1.ex: 잠깐 "heads up"인데, 회의가 일찍 시작돼.

facts.def: Used when something doesn't seem logical.

example.text: This game rule makes no sense.

misuse.text: Don't say 'makes no sense' about your boss's plan.

l1.hook: 규칙이 또 바뀌었어. 왜? 전혀 'makes no sense'야.
l1.ex: 이 게임 규칙은 "makes no sense".

facts.def: Something unfair said to hurt someone.

example.text: That joke was a low blow.

misuse.text: Don't call fair criticism a 'low blow'.
misuse.why: It may just be honest feedback.

l1.hook: 그가 그녀의 옛 실수를 언급했어! "low blow".
l1.ex: 그 농담은 "low blow"였어.

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: A melhor pizza da cidade. Acredite, "no cap".
l1.ex: Esta pizza é a melhor da cidade, "no cap".

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: Ele perdeu e ficou "salty".
l1.ex: Ele está "salty" porque eu ganhei o jogo de cartas.

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: O gato pulou na caixa! "I'm dead".
l1.ex: O gato pulou na caixa. "I'm dead"!

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.hook: A pizza inteira acabou! "pig out".
l1.ex: Nós nos empanturramos de pizza ontem à noite (fizemos um "pig out").

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: Pizza às seis, "bet"?
l1.ex: Pizza às seis? "Bet".

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: Pizza e filme de novo? "basic"
l1.ex: Meu plano de fim de semana é "basic": pizza e filme.

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: Aqueles dois pararam de conversar. Por quê? "beef"
l1.ex: Eles têm "beef" por causa de um jogo.

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: Seu quarto parece do Pinterest! "aesthetic"
l1.ex: Sua escrivaninha está tão "aesthetic".

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: A massa da mãe está incrível esta noite! "bussin"
l1.ex: A massa da mãe está "bussin" hoje à noite.

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: Obrigado(a) pela carona! ("anytime")
l1.ex: Obrigado pela carona! "anytime".

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: Cinco minutos, depois eu volto! "AFK"
l1.ex: Volto já, vou ficar "AFK" por cinco minutos.

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: Onde a chave foi? ("beats me")
l1.ex: Onde está a chave? "beats me".

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: O plano falhou. E agora, "back to square one"?
l1.ex: Plano falhou. "back to square one".

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: Olha o preço deste casaco! É "arm and a leg".
l1.ex: Este casaco custa "arm and a leg".

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: Ah, "by the way", tem mais uma coisa!
l1.ex: "By the way", a festa começa às sete.

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: Você conseguiu ingressos grátis para a gente?
l1.ex: Você conseguiu ingressos grátis para a gente? Isso é "awesome"!

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: Gato sonolento. Exatamente como me sinto!
l1.ex: Aquele gato sonolento é um "big mood".

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.hook: Dia de prova. Como foi?
l1.ex: Eu "ace"i meu teste de história hoje!

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.
