example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: Fim de semana chuvoso. Toda a temporada. Vamos!
l1.ex: Eu vou "binge-watch" esta série o fim de semana inteiro.

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: Muito trabalho. Estou "burned out"!
l1.ex: Depois das provas, eu me senti totalmente "burned out".

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: Na semana passada estava doente, hoje estou "back on my feet"!
l1.ex: Finalmente estou "back on my feet".

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: Preciso disso agora, "ASAP"!
l1.ex: Por favor, envie-me as notas "ASAP".

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: Filme hoje à noite às seis, "cool"?
l1.ex: "Cool", nos vemos às seis!

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: Ele nunca paga o almoço, é "cheap"!
l1.ex: Ele é "cheap" demais para comprar o almoço.

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.hook: Ela contou a todos o meu erro! ("call out")
l1.ex: Ela me chamou a atenção ("called me out") por estar atrasado.

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.hook: Dia de entrevista. Terno e gravata! "dressed to impress"
l1.ex: Ele está "dressed to impress" para a entrevista.

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.hook: Duas horas dos mesmos slides! "bored stiff"
l1.ex: Eu estava "bored stiff" naquela aula.

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.hook: Sábado. Dieta? Que dieta? "cheat day"
l1.ex: Sábado é o meu "cheat day"

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.hook: Quem conhece todos os seus segredos? "bestie"
l1.ex: Minha "bestie" e eu adoramos tacos.

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.hook: Você passou no teste? "big W"!
l1.ex: Você passou no teste? "big W"!

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.hook: Pizza com abacaxi é a melhor! "hot take"
l1.ex: Aqui vai meu "hot take": abacaxi combina com pizza.

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: Ele tropeçou na peça da escola! "blooper"
l1.ex: Esse "blooper" fez toda a classe rir.

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.hook: Quanto vai custar? "ballpark figure"
l1.ex: Me dê um "ballpark figure".

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.hook: Noite de jogos aqui em casa! "count me in"
l1.ex: Noite de jogos? "count me in"!

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.hook: Toque essa música mais alto!
l1.ex: Essa nova música é um "banger"!

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

l1.hook: Meias com sandálias? Sério?
l1.ex: Meias com sandálias? "Big yikes".

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

l1.hook: Luzes do palco acesas. Minha mente está vazia!
l1.ex: Eu tive um "blank out" no meio do meu discurso.

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

l1.hook: Três horas de vídeos bobos!
l1.ex: Muitos vídeos me dão "brain rot".

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

l1.hook: Sem tempo livre esta semana!
l1.ex: Estou "busy as a bee" esta semana.

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

l1.hook: Está congelando lá fora. Pronto para 'bundle up'?
l1.ex: "Bundle up", está congelando lá fora!

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

l1.hook: Não há tempo agora. 'circle back' depois?
l1.ex: Vamos "circle back" nisso depois do almoço.

facts.def: Used to accept someone's point.

example.text: Fair enough, let's try your idea.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fair enough' to a rude insult.
misuse.why: It sounds like you agree with them.

l1.hook: Espere, ouça meu raciocínio primeiro. 'fair enough'?
l1.ex: "Fair enough", vamos tentar sua ideia.

facts.def: Describes things that are corny or too sweet.

example.text: That movie was so cheesy.

misuse.text: Don't call her poem 'cheesy' at the party.
misuse.why: It sounds mean about heartfelt effort.

l1.hook: A nota de amor dele rimou. Que "cheesy"!
l1.ex: Esse filme era tão "cheesy".

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

l1.hook: Nova jaqueta, novos sapatos, nova confiança! 'drip'
l1.ex: Jaqueta legal, você está com "drip" hoje.

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: Viagem cancelada. Todo mundo está 'bummed out'!
l1.ex: Estou "bummed out" com a viagem.

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

l1.hook: Prove isso e me diga. 'chef's kiss'
l1.ex: A sopa estava "chef's kiss".

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

l1.hook: Valeu, 'bro', por salvar minha lição de casa!
l1.ex: Obrigado, "bro", você me salvou!

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

l1.hook: Eu comi seu bolo!
l1.ex: Eu comi seu bolo! "just kidding".

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

l1.hook: Esqueci minhas anotações. Ah não!
l1.ex: Esqueci minhas anotações. Estou "cooked".

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

l1.hook: Ela só bebe chá "bougie"!
l1.ex: Esta cafeteria é tão "bougie".

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

l1.hook: Quer ir ao late show?
l1.ex: Estou cansado, então "count me out".

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: Ele agradeceu a todos, até aos rivais!
l1.ex: Nosso treinador é um verdadeiro "class act".

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: "bruh", você esqueceu a lição de casa de novo?
l1.ex: Bruh, você esqueceu a lição de casa de novo?

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.hook: O grupo de chat explodiu por nada! "drama"
l1.ex: Eu não quero nenhum "drama" este ano.

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.hook: Ela parece triste. E agora? "cheer up"
l1.ex: "Cheer up", vamos comer pizza!

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.hook: Dia triste? Sopa quente! "comfort food"
l1.ex: Sopa quente é meu "comfort food".

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: Quem estuda com você todas as noites? "buddy"
l1.ex: Ele é meu "buddy" de estudo.

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.hook: Gol de último segundo garante a vitória! "clutch"
l1.ex: Aquele gol de última hora foi muito "clutch".

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: Essa loja é legit?
l1.ex: Essa loja é "legit", minha irmã comprou sapatos lá.

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

l1.hook: Sou novo. Por favor, seja gentil! "cut me some slack"
l1.ex: "Cut me some slack", sou novo.

facts.def: To cost so much that you can't afford it.

example.text: Don't worry, this lunch won't break the bank.

misuse.text: Don't say 'break the bank' at a bank.
misuse.why: It only means costing too much.

l1.hook: Almoço está caro demais? "break the bank"
l1.ex: Não se preocupe, esse almoço não vai "break the bank".

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: Passe aqui a qualquer hora esta semana! "drop by"
l1.ex: Sinta-se à vontade para dar uma passada ("drop by") a qualquer momento.

facts.def: Used when someone is doing really well at something.

example.text: You're crushing it at your new job!

misuse.text: Don't tell a struggling friend 'crushing it' sarcastically.

l1.hook: Primeira semana e já é o mais vendido! Você está "crushing it".
l1.ex: Você está arrasando ("crushing it") no seu emprego novo!

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: A viagem foi cancelada. Que chato! "bummer".
l1.ex: A viagem foi cancelada? Que "bummer".

facts.def: To study many things quickly just before a test.

example.text: I must cram for math.

misuse.text: Don't 'cram' for a three-year course.
misuse.why: Cramming only works for short tests.

l1.hook: Prova amanhã. Ainda não estudei! Preciso "cram".
l1.ex: Preciso "cram" para matemática.

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: Já é tarde e estou com sono! Preciso "catch some Zs".
l1.ex: Eu vou "catch some Zs".

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

l1.hook: Um cochilo, e já estou "good as new".
l1.ex: Depois de um cochilo, me sinto "good as new".

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

l1.hook: A reunião começa. Quem vai "get the ball rolling" primeiro?
l1.ex: Vamos "get the ball rolling" com algumas ideias.

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

l1.hook: Posso contar com você?
l1.ex: Pizza hoje à noite? "For sure"!

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

l1.hook: A festa acabou às oito. É sério?
l1.ex: Aquela festa foi meio "lame".

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

l1.hook: Nós sorrimos, mas competimos!
l1.ex: Ela é minha "frenemy", sempre competindo comigo.

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: Dia difícil, mas o amanhã está vindo!
l1.ex: "Chin up", amanhã será melhor.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: O jantar está pronto. Quem está com fome? Vamos "dig in"!
l1.ex: O jantar está pronto, então "dig in"!

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: Tenho que ir. A aula começa agora! "catch you later"
l1.ex: "Catch you later", eu preciso ir!

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: Gol de último segundo. Nós ganhamos! "epic win"
l1.ex: Nós marcamos no último segundo. "Epic win"!

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

l1.hook: Opinião sincera sobre esse filme? "ngl"
l1.ex: "Ngl", eu amei aquele filme.

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: Meu bolo desabou. Todos assistiram! "epic fail"
l1.ex: Meu bolo solou. Um verdadeiro "epic fail"!

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

l1.hook: Presente para ela? Alguém se habilita a "chip in"?
l1.ex: Vamos todos "chip in" para o presente dela.

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: Prova amanhã. Qual é o nosso "game plan"?
l1.ex: E aí, qual é o "game plan"?

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

l1.hook: Olha meus tênis novos! "fire"
l1.ex: Esses tênis são "fire"!

facts.def: A casual way to ask someone to repeat.

example.text: Come again? It's too loud here.

misuse.text: Don't say 'come again' when you heard clearly.

l1.hook: Desculpa, a música está muito alta! "come again"
l1.ex: "come again"? Está muito barulhento aqui.

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

l1.hook: Provas finais semana que vem. Hora de "hit the books"!
l1.ex: Eu tenho que "hit the books" hoje à noite.

facts.def: People who love the same show or band.

example.text: The fandom loves this band.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers a 'fandom'.
misuse.why: It means devoted fans of one thing.

l1.hook: Quem ama mais essa banda? "fandom"
l1.ex: O "fandom" ama essa banda.

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

l1.hook: Essa caminhada pareceu interminável! "dog tired"
l1.ex: Eu estou "dog tired" depois dessa longa caminhada.

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: Olha lá fora! Pegue o guarda-chuva! "raining cats and dogs"
l1.ex: Está "raining cats and dogs"!

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

l1.hook: Heads up: o chefe está chegando!
l1.ex: Só um "heads up", a reunião vai começar mais cedo.

facts.def: Used when something doesn't seem logical.

example.text: This game rule makes no sense.

misuse.text: Don't say 'makes no sense' about your boss's plan.

l1.hook: As regras mudaram de novo. Por quê?
l1.ex: Esta regra do jogo "makes no sense" (não faz sentido nenhum).

facts.def: Something unfair said to hurt someone.

example.text: That joke was a low blow.

misuse.text: Don't call fair criticism a 'low blow'.
misuse.why: It may just be honest feedback.

l1.hook: Low blow: ele mencionou o erro antigo dela!
l1.ex: Aquela piada foi um "low blow" (golpe baixo).

facts.mean: Succeed at wearing or doing something bold.
facts.def: To manage something hard or bold, like a style.

example.text: Not everyone can pull off that color.

misuse.text: Don't say 'pull off' when you mean 'remove'.

l1.hook: Quem mais veste aquilo?
l1.ex: Nem todo mundo consegue "pull off" (segurar o tchan de / ficar bem com) essa cor.

facts.mean: Grumpy and in a bad mood.
facts.def: Describes someone tired or annoyed.

example.text: I'm cranky before breakfast.

misuse.text: Don't call your boss 'cranky' in an email.

l1.hook: Não fala comigo ainda!
l1.ex: Eu fico "cranky" (rabugento/mal-humorado) antes do café da manhã.

facts.mean: A person who loves good food.
facts.def: Someone who enjoys trying and talking about food.
facts.hook: She reviews every restaurant in town!

example.text: My sister is a total foodie.

misuse.text: Don't call a chef a 'foodie'.
misuse.why: A chef cooks; a foodie loves eating.

l1.hook: Ela faz resenha de todos os restaurantes da cidade!
l1.ex: Minha irmã é uma total "foodie".

facts.def: A British way to say thank you or goodbye.
facts.hook: He held the door. Say thanks!

example.text: Cheers for the lift!

misuse.text: Don't expect Americans to understand 'cheers' as thanks.

l1.hook: Ele segurou a porta. Diga cheers!
l1.ex: Cheers pela carona!

facts.def: Said politely after a match ends.

example.text: GG, that was a fun match!

misuse.text: Don't type 'GG' to your boss after a project.

l1.hook: A partida acabou. GG?
l1.ex: GG, foi uma partida divertida!

facts.def: A hand-on-face gesture of disbelief.

example.text: My phone was in my hand. Facepalm!

misuse.text: Don't 'facepalm' at your teacher's answer.

l1.hook: Ele procurou o telefone! Facepalm!
l1.ex: Meu telefone estava na minha mão. Facepalm!

facts.def: Used when you have almost no money at all.

example.text: I'm flat broke until Friday.

misuse.text: Don't say 'flat broke' about a broken phone.

l1.hook: Flat broke: posso pegar dez dólares emprestado?
l1.ex: Estou flat broke até sexta-feira.

facts.def: To contact someone by text or call.

example.text: Hit me up if you need help.

misuse.text: Don't say 'hit me up' to your professor.

l1.hook: Precisa de ajuda? Estou por aqui! Hit me up.
l1.ex: Hit me up se precisar de ajuda.

facts.mean: A big change for the better.
facts.def: A big improvement in how someone looks, feels or lives.

example.text: Wow, your glow-up this year is amazing.

misuse.text: Don't tell someone their glow-up means they looked bad.
misuse.why: It implies they looked bad before.

l1.hook: Ano passado vs este ano! Glow-up.
l1.ex: Uau, seu glow-up este ano está incrível.

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: Лучшая пицца в городе. Поверьте, no cap.
l1.ex: Эта пицца — лучшая в городе, no cap.

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: Он проиграл, а потом стал salty.
l1.ex: Он salty, потому что я выиграл в карточную игру.

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: Кот прыгнул в коробку! I'm dead.
l1.ex: Кот прыгнул в коробку. I'm dead!

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: Пицца в шесть, bet?
l1.ex: Пицца в шесть? Bet.

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: Опять пицца и фильм?
l1.ex: Мой план на выходные "basic": пицца и фильм.

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: Эти двое перестали разговаривать. Почему?
l1.ex: У них "beef" из‑за игры.

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: Твоя комната выглядит как в Pinterest!
l1.ex: Твой стол выглядит так "aesthetic".

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.hook: Папа увидел беспорядок в комнате!
l1.ex: Он «blow a fuse» из‑за беспорядка в комнате.

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: Паста мамы сегодня просто нереальная!
l1.ex: Паста мамы "bussin" сегодня.

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: Спасибо большое за поездку! «anytime».
l1.ex: Спасибо за поездку! Anytime.

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: Пять минут, потом я вернусь! «AFK».
l1.ex: Brb, я буду AFK пять минут.

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: Куда делся ключ? «beats me».
l1.ex: Где ключ? Beats me.

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: План провалился. Что дальше? «back to square one».
l1.ex: План провалился. Back to square one.

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: Посмотри на цену этого пальто! «arm and a leg».
l1.ex: Это пальто стоит an arm and a leg.

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: О, ещё одна вещь! «by the way».
l1.ex: «By the way», вечеринка начинается в семь.

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: Ты достал нам бесплатные билеты?
l1.ex: Ты достал нам бесплатные билеты? Это «awesome»!

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: Сонный кот. Точно мои чувства!
l1.ex: Тот сонный кот — это «big mood».

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.hook: День теста. Как у тебя получилось?
l1.ex: Я сегодня «aced» тест по истории!

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: Дождливые выходные. Весь сезон. Поехали!
l1.ex: Я буду «binge-watch» этот сериал весь уикенд.

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: Слишком много работы. Я «burned out»!
l1.ex: После экзаменов я почувствовал себя полностью «burned out».

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: На прошлой неделе болел, сегодня уже «back on my feet»!
l1.ex: Я наконец‑то «back on my feet».

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: Мне это нужно прямо сейчас, «ASAP»!
l1.ex: Пожалуйста, пришлите мне заметки ASAP.

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: Фильм сегодня в шесть, «cool»?
l1.ex: «Cool», увидимся в шесть!

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: Он никогда не платит за обед, «cheap»!
l1.ex: Он слишком «cheap», чтобы купить обед.

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.hook: Она всем рассказала о моей ошибке! «call out».
l1.ex: Она сделала мне замечание («called me out») за то, что я опоздал.

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.hook: День интервью. Костюм и галстук — «dressed to impress».
l1.ex: Он "dressed to impress" для интервью.

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.hook: Два часа одних и тех же слайдов — «bored stiff».
l1.ex: Я был "bored stiff" на том уроке.

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.hook: Суббота. Диета? Какая диета? — «cheat day».
l1.ex: Суббота — мой «cheat day».

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.hook: Кто знает все твои секреты? — «bestie».
l1.ex: Моя «bestie» и я любим тако.

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.hook: Ты сдал тест? «big W»!
l1.ex: Ты сдал тест? «Big W»!

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.hook: «hot take» — ананасовая пицца лучшая!
l1.ex: Вот мой «hot take»: ананас должен быть на пицце.

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: Он споткнулся в школьном спектакле! «blooper»
l1.ex: Этот «blooper» заставил весь класс смеяться.

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.hook: Сколько это будет стоить? «ballpark figure»
l1.ex: Дай мне «ballpark figure».

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.hook: Вечер игр у меня дома! «count me in»
l1.ex: Вечер игр? «Count me in»!

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.hook: Включи эту песню погромче! «banger»
l1.ex: Эта новая песня — "banger"!

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: Он поблагодарил всех, даже соперников! («class act»)
l1.ex: Наш тренер — настоящий «class act».

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: Ты опять забыл домашнее задание? («bruh»)
l1.ex: «Bruh», ты снова забыл домашку?

facts.def: To keep working late into the night.

example.text: We burned the midnight oil last night.

misuse.text: Don't say it about lighting candles.

l1.hook: Ты всё ещё работаешь в два часа ночи? («burn the midnight oil»)
l1.ex: Прошлой ночью нам пришлось «burn the midnight oil».

facts.mean: A title that tricks you to click.
facts.def: A catchy headline that isn't worth reading.

example.text: That title is pure clickbait.

misuse.text: Don't call a real news story 'clickbait'.

l1.hook: «Ты не поверишь!» — правда? («clickbait»)
l1.ex: Этот заголовок — чистый clickbait.

facts.def: To decide to finish work or an activity for now.

example.text: We're tired, let's call it a day.

misuse.text: Don't 'call it a day' before the deadline.

l1.hook: Мы устали. Что дальше?
l1.ex: Мы устали, давай «call it a day».

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

l1.hook: Просто небольшие новости!
l1.ex: FYI, магазин закрывается в пять.

facts.def: Used to say you accept an idea.

example.text: Pizza or tacos? Fine by me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fine by me' when you're upset.
misuse.why: People will think you truly don't mind.

l1.hook: Пицца или тако, выбирай.
l1.ex: Пицца или тако? «fine by me».

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

l1.hook: Опять папина шутка. Серьёзно?
l1.ex: Шутки папы такие «corny».

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.hook: В групповом чате начался «drama» из‑за ничего.
l1.ex: Я не хочу никакого «drama» в этом году.

facts.def: A moment to show your outfit and get opinions.

example.text: Quick fit check before school!

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'fit check' at the gym.

l1.hook: Наряд готов. Что думаешь перед школой? («fit check»)
l1.ex: Быстрый «fit check» перед школой!

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.hook: Она выглядит грустной. Что дальше? («cheer up»)
l1.ex: «Cheer up», у нас будет пицца!

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.hook: Грустный день? Тёплый суп — «comfort food».
l1.ex: Тёплый суп — мой «comfort food».

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: Кто твой «buddy», который учится с тобой каждую ночь?
l1.ex: Он мой учебный «buddy».

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.hook: Гол в последнюю секунду решает всё! («clutch»)
l1.ex: Тот гол в последнюю минуту был таким «clutch».

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: Этот магазин «legit»?
l1.ex: Этот магазин «legit», моя сестра купила там обувь.

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: Заходи в любое время на этой неделе, «drop by»!
l1.ex: Не стесняйтесь «drop by» в любое время.

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: Поездка отменена. «bummer»!
l1.ex: Поездка отменена? Какой «bummer».

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: Поздно, и я хочу «catch some Zs».
l1.ex: Я собираюсь «catch some Zs».

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: Эта куртка «it's giving» атмосферу старых фильмов!
l1.ex: Эта куртка «it's giving» образ старой кинозвезды.

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: Тяжёлый день, но «chin up», завтра уже наступит!
l1.ex: «Chin up», завтра будет лучше.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: Ужин готов. Кто голоден? «dig in».
l1.ex: Ужин готов, так что «dig in»!

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.hook: Надо идти, сейчас начинается урок! «catch you later».
l1.ex: «Catch you later», мне нужно идти!

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.hook: Гол в последнюю секунду. Мы выиграли! «epic win».
l1.ex: Мы забили в последнюю секунду. «Epic win!»

facts.mean: Grumpy and in a bad mood.
facts.def: Describes someone tired or annoyed.

example.text: I'm cranky before breakfast.

misuse.text: Don't call your boss 'cranky' in an email.

l1.hook: Не разговаривай со мной пока, я «cranky»!
l1.ex: Я «cranky» до завтрака.

facts.mean: A person who loves good food.
facts.def: Someone who enjoys trying and talking about food.
facts.hook: She reviews every restaurant in town!

example.text: My sister is a total foodie.

misuse.text: Don't call a chef a 'foodie'.
misuse.why: A chef cooks; a foodie loves eating.

l1.hook: Она «foodie», она пробует каждый ресторан в городе!
l1.ex: Моя сестра — абсолютная «foodie».

facts.def: A British way to say thank you or goodbye.
facts.hook: He held the door. Say thanks!

example.text: Cheers for the lift!

misuse.text: Don't expect Americans to understand 'cheers' as thanks.

l1.hook: Он держал дверь. Скажи «cheers»!
l1.ex: «Cheers» за то, что подвёз!

facts.def: Said politely after a match ends.

example.text: GG, that was a fun match!

misuse.text: Don't type 'GG' to your boss after a project.

l1.hook: Матч только что закончился. «GG»?
l1.ex: «GG», это была весёлая игра!

facts.def: A hand-on-face gesture of disbelief.

example.text: My phone was in my hand. Facepalm!

misuse.text: Don't 'facepalm' at your teacher's answer.

l1.hook: Он искал свой телефон! «facepalm»
l1.ex: Мой телефон был в руке. Facepalm!

facts.def: Used when you have almost no money at all.

example.text: I'm flat broke until Friday.

misuse.text: Don't say 'flat broke' about a broken phone.

l1.hook: Можно одолжить десять долларов?
l1.ex: Я «flat broke» до пятницы.

facts.def: To contact someone by text or call.

example.text: Hit me up if you need help.

misuse.text: Don't say 'hit me up' to your professor.

l1.hook: Нужна помощь? Я рядом!
l1.ex: Hit me up, если тебе нужна помощь.

facts.mean: A big change for the better.
facts.def: A big improvement in how someone looks, feels or lives.

example.text: Wow, your glow-up this year is amazing.

misuse.text: Don't tell someone their glow-up means they looked bad.
misuse.why: It implies they looked bad before.

l1.hook: В прошлом году и в этом году!
l1.ex: Wow, твой glow-up в этом году потрясающий.

facts.def: Used when something is so funny you can't stop laughing.

example.text: We were cracking up at his joke.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cracking up' about a cracked phone.

l1.hook: Его шутка была нелепой!
l1.ex: Мы «cracking up» от его шутки.

facts.def: Used when something is too confusing to understand.

example.text: This homework is all Greek to me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's all Greek to me' about easy tasks.

l1.hook: Домашка по математике? Я в растерянности!
l1.ex: Это домашнее задание — для меня «it's all Greek to me».

facts.mean: Show off something you're proud of.
facts.def: To show off what you have or can do.

example.text: He keeps flexing his new sneakers online.

misuse.text: Don't 'flex' your salary at a job interview.

l1.hook: Он постоянно «flex» свои кроссовки!
l1.ex: Он всё время «flex» свои новые кроссовки онлайн.

facts.mean: A person who wakes up early.
facts.def: Someone who likes to get up and start early.

example.text: My dad is an early bird.

misuse.text: Don't call a late sleeper an 'early bird'.
misuse.why: It means someone who wakes early.

l1.hook: Мой папа встаёт в пять! Он «early bird».
l1.ex: Мой папа — «early bird».

facts.def: A day with extremely hot weather.

example.text: Today is a real scorcher!

misuse.text: Don't say 'scorcher' about a cold morning.
misuse.why: It means a very hot day.

l1.hook: Солнце палит. Даже в тени жарко — это «scorcher».
l1.ex: Сегодня настоящий «scorcher»!

facts.def: Being included and informed about what's going on.

example.text: Keep me in the loop about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'in the loop' about a roller coaster.
misuse.why: It means knowing the latest news.

l1.hook: Никто не сказал мне новости, я не в «in the loop».
l1.ex: Держи меня в «in the loop» по поводу поездки.

facts.def: A polite way to say no or that you're okay.

example.text: No thanks, I'm good.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm good' if you want more food.

l1.hook: Хочешь ещё кусок торта? — «I'm good».
l1.ex: Нет, спасибо, I'm good.

facts.def: Used to show you aren't impressed.

example.text: The movie? Meh.

misuse.text: Don't say 'meh' about a friend's cooking.

l1.hook: Как тебе фильм?
l1.ex: Фильм? Meh.

facts.def: Used for someone who makes a big deal out of small things.

example.text: Counting every cookie is petty, don't you think?

misuse.text: Don't call a real complaint 'petty'.

l1.hook: Он хочет вернуть своё печенье?
l1.ex: Считать каждое печенье petty, не так ли?

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.m: ไม่ได้โกหกนะ
l1.hook: พิซซ่าอร่อยที่สุดในเมืองเลย เชื่อฉันนะ no cap
l1.ex: พิซซ่านี้อร่อยที่สุดในเมือง, no cap

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: เขาแพ้แล้วก็ "salty"!
l1.ex: เขา salty เพราะฉันชนะเกมไพ่

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: แมวกระโดดเข้าไปในกล่องเลย "I'm dead"
l1.ex: แมวกระโดดเข้าไปในกล่อง ฉันหัวเราะจน 'I'm dead'!

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.m: กินเยอะเกินไป
l1.hook: พิซซ่าทั้งหมดหายไปแล้ว "pig out"
l1.ex: เรากินพิซซ่าอย่าง "pig out" เมื่อคืน

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: พิซซ่าเวลา 6 โมง ดีไหม? "bet"
l1.ex: พิซซ่าเวลา 6 โมง? Bet

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: พิซซ่าและหนังอีกแล้ว?
l1.ex: แผนวันหยุดของฉัน "basic": พิซซ่าและหนัง

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.m: ความขัดแย้ง
l1.hook: คนสองคนนั้นหยุดคุยกันแล้ว ทำไม?
l1.ex: พวกเขามี "beef" เกี่ยวกับเกม

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: ห้องของคุณดูเหมือน Pinterest!
l1.ex: โต๊ะทำงานของคุณดู "aesthetic" มาก

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.m: ระเบิดอารมณ์
l1.hook: พ่อเห็นห้องรก!
l1.ex: เขา "blow a fuse" เมื่อเห็นห้องรก

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: พาสต้าแม่อร่อยเกินจริงคืนนี้!
l1.ex: พาสต้าแม่ "bussin" คืนนี้

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: ขอบคุณมากสำหรับการพาไป! "anytime"
l1.ex: ขอบคุณที่ให้ขับรถ! "anytime".

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.m: ไม่ได้อยู่หน้าจอ
l1.hook: ห้านาทีแล้วฉันจะกลับมา! "AFK"
l1.ex: เดี๋ยวกลับนะ ฉันจะ "AFK" ห้านาที.

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.m: ฉันก็ไม่รู้เหมือนกัน
l1.hook: กุญแจหายไปไหน? 'beats me'!
l1.ex: กุญแจหายไปไหน? "beats me".

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.m: กลับไปนับหนึ่งใหม่
l1.hook: แผนล้มเหลว แล้วตอนนี้ทำอย่างไร 'back to square one'!
l1.ex: แผนล้มเหลว "back to square one".

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: ดูราคาของเสื้อโค้ทนี้สิ 'arm and a leg'!
l1.ex: เสื้อโค้ทนี้ราคา "arm and a leg".

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: โอ้ "by the way" อีกเรื่องหนึ่ง!
l1.ex: "by the way" ปาร์ตี้เริ่มตอนเจ็ดโมง.

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: คุณได้ตั๋วฟรีให้เราหรือ?
l1.ex: คุณได้ตั๋วฟรีให้เราหรือ? นั่น "awesome"!

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: แมวนอนหลับ เหมือนความรู้สึกของฉันเลย!
l1.ex: แมวนอนหลับนั้นเป็น "big mood".

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.m: ทำได้ดีเยี่ยม
l1.hook: วันสอบ คุณทำอย่างไรบ้าง?
l1.ex: ฉัน "ace" การสอบประวัติศาสตร์วันนี้!

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.m: ดูรวดเดียวจบ
l1.hook: วันหยุดฝนตก ทั้งซีซั่น ไปเลย!
l1.ex: ฉันจะ "binge-watch" รายการนี้ตลอดสุดสัปดาห์.

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: งานเยอะเกินไป ฉันรู้สึก “burned out” แล้ว!
l1.ex: หลังสอบ ฉันรู้สึก “burned out” อย่างเต็มที่.

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: อาทิตย์ที่แล้วป่วย วันนี้ฉัน “back on my feet” แล้ว!
l1.ex: ฉัน “back on my feet” แล้ว.

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: ฉันต้องการมันเดี๋ยวนี้! ส่งให้ “ASAP” นะ
l1.ex: กรุณาส่งโน้ตให้ฉัน “ASAP” นะ

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: หนังคืนนี้หกโมง ตกลงไหม? “cool”
l1.ex: “cool”, แล้วเจอกันตอนหกโมง!

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.m: ขี้ประหยัด
l1.hook: เขาไม่เคยจ่ายค่าอาหารกลางวันเลย! เขา “cheap”
l1.ex: เขา “cheap” จนไม่ซื้ออาหารกลางวัน

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.m: ชี้ข้อผิดพลาด
l1.hook: เธอ 'call out' ความผิดของฉันต่อทุกคน!
l1.ex: เธอ 'call out' ฉันเพราะมาสาย

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.m: แต่งตัวให้ดูดี
l1.hook: วันสัมภาษณ์ 'dressed to impress' ใส่สูทและเนคไท!
l1.ex: เขา 'dressed to impress' สำหรับการสัมภาษณ์

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

l1.m: เบื่อจนตาย
l1.hook: สองชั่วโมงของสไลด์เดียวกัน 'bored stiff'!
l1.ex: ฉัน 'bored stiff' ในชั้นเรียนนั้น

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

l1.m: วันละเมิดไดเอท
l1.hook: วันเสาร์ 'cheat day' ไดเอท? ไดเอทอะไร?
l1.ex: วันเสาร์เป็น 'cheat day' ของฉัน

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

l1.m: เพื่อนสนิท
l1.hook: ใครคือ 'bestie' ที่รู้ทุกความลับของคุณ?
l1.ex: ฉันและ 'bestie' ของฉันชอบทาโก้

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

l1.m: ชัยชนะครั้งใหญ่
l1.hook: คุณสอบผ่านแล้วหรือ? "big W"!
l1.ex: คุณสอบผ่านแล้วหรือ? Big W!

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

l1.m: มุมมองสุดโดดเด่น
l1.hook: พิซซ่าใส่สับปะรดอร่อยที่สุด "hot take"!
l1.ex: นี่คือ "hot take" ของฉัน: สับปะรดควรอยู่บนพิซซ่า.

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

l1.hook: เขาล้มในละครโรงเรียน! "blooper"
l1.ex: "blooper" นั้นทำให้ทั้งชั้นหัวเราะ.

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

l1.m: ตัวเลขคร่าวๆ
l1.hook: ค่าใช้จ่ายประมาณเท่าไหร่? 'ballpark figure'!
l1.ex: บอก "ballpark figure" ให้หน่อย.

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

l1.m: นับฉันด้วย
l1.hook: คืนเกมที่บ้านฉัน! "count me in"
l1.ex: คืนเกม? Count me in!

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

l1.m: เพลงฮิตติดหู
l1.hook: เปิดเพลงนี้ให้ดังขึ้น! "banger"
l1.ex: เพลงใหม่เพลงนี้เป็น "banger"!

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

l1.hook: ถุงเท้ากับรองเท้าแตะ? จริงเหรอ? big yikes
l1.ex: ใส่ถุงเท้ากับรองเท้าแตะ? "big yikes".

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

l1.m: นึกไม่ออกกะทันหัน
l1.hook: ไฟบนเวทีเปิดแล้ว. ใจฉันว่างเปล่า! blank out
l1.ex: ฉัน "blank out" ตอนกลางสุนทรพจน์ของฉัน.

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

l1.m: คอนเทนต์ไร้สาระ
l1.hook: ดูวิดีโอตลกเป็นเวลาสามชั่วโมง! brain rot
l1.ex: วิดีโอมากเกินไปทำให้ฉัน "brain rot".

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

l1.m: ทำงานอย่างผึ้ง
l1.hook: สัปดาห์นี้ไม่มีเวลาว่าง! busy as a bee
l1.ex: ฉัน "busy as a bee" สัปดาห์นี้.

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

l1.m: สวมเสื้อผ้าหนาๆ
l1.hook: อากาศหนาวมากเลยนะ "bundle up" พร้อมไหม?
l1.ex: Bundle up, อากาศหนาวมากข้างนอก!

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

l1.m: กลับมาพูดเรื่องนั้น
l1.hook: ตอนนี้ไม่มีเวลา "circle back" ไหม?
l1.ex: หลังอาหารกลางวัน เรา "circle back" ไปที่เรื่องนั้นกันเถอะ

facts.def: To answer criticism quickly and cleverly.

example.text: She clapped back with a great reply.

misuse.text: Don't 'clap back' at a parent's advice.

l1.m: ตอบโต้อย่างเฉียบคม
l1.hook: เขาล้อเลียนเธอ เธอตอบกลับด้วย "clap back"!
l1.ex: เธอ "clap back" ด้วยการตอบที่ยอดเยี่ยม

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

l1.hook: แจ็คเก็ตใหม่ รองเท้าใหม่ ความมั่นใจใหม่ "drip"!
l1.ex: แจ็คเก็ตดีนะ, วันนี้เธอมี "drip" เลย.

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.hook: ทริปถูกยกเลิก ทุกคนเศร้า "bummed out"!
l1.ex: ฉันรู้สึก "bummed out" เกี่ยวกับทริปนี้.

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

l1.hook: ลองชิมนี่แล้วบอกฉัน "chef's kiss"!
l1.ex: ซุปนี้เป็น "chef's kiss" เลย.

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

l1.hook: ขอบคุณที่ช่วยเก็บการบ้านของฉัน "bro"!
l1.ex: ขอบคุณ, "bro", คุณช่วยฉันได้แล้ว!

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

l1.m: ล้อเล่นน่า
l1.hook: ฉันกินเค้กของคุณ!
l1.ex: ฉันกินเค้กของคุณ. "just kidding"

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

l1.hook: ฉันลืมโน้ตของฉัน. อุ๊
l1.ex: ฉันลืมโน้ตของฉัน. "cooked"

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

l1.hook: เธอดื่มชาแบบหรูหราเท่านั้น!
l1.ex: ร้านกาแฟนี้ "bougie" มาก

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

l1.hook: อยากไปดูการแสดงดึกไหม?
l1.ex: ฉันเหนื่อย, ดังนั้น "count me out"

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

l1.hook: เขาขอบคุณทุกคน, แม้แต่คู่แข่ง!
l1.ex: โค้ชของเราคือ "class act" จริงๆ

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

l1.hook: bruh, ทำการบ้านลืมอีกแล้วหรือ?
l1.ex: Bruh, คุณลืมการบ้านอีกแล้วหรือ?

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

l1.hook: FYI, แค่ข่าวเล็กน้อย!
l1.ex: FYI, ร้านปิดตอนห้าโมงเย็น.

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

l1.hook: 'corny' มุขพ่ออีกแล้ว. จริงๆ?
l1.ex: มุขของพ่อมัน "corny" มากเลย.

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

l1.m: เรื่องวุ่นวาย
l1.hook: กลุ่มแชทเกิด drama กันเพราะเรื่องไม่มีสาระ!
l1.ex: ฉันไม่อยากมี "drama" ใด ๆ ปีนี้.

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

l1.m: ร่าเริงหน่อย
l1.hook: เธอดูเศร้าเลย จะทำยังไงต่อ?
l1.ex: "Cheer up", เรากำลังกินพิซซ่า!

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

l1.m: อาหารปลอบใจ
l1.hook: วันเศร้า? ซุปอุ่นๆ!
l1.ex: ซุปอุ่นคือ "comfort food" ของฉัน.

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

l1.hook: ใครเรียนกับคุณทุกคืน?
l1.ex: เขาเป็น "buddy" ของฉันในการเรียน.

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

l1.hook: ประตูในวินาทีสุดท้ายทำให้ชนะ!
l1.ex: ประตูในนาทีสุดท้ายนั้น "clutch" มาก.

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

l1.hook: ร้านนี้จริงหรือ?
l1.ex: ร้านนี้ "legit" นะ พี่สาวของฉันซื้อรองเท้าที่นั่น.

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

l1.m: ผ่อนปรนให้หน่อย
l1.hook: ฉันใหม่ ช่วย cut me some slack หน่อย
l1.ex: "Cut me some slack", ฉันเพิ่งเริ่มใหม่

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

l1.hook: สัปดาห์นี้มา drop by ได้ทุกเวลา!
l1.ex: คุณสามารถ "drop by" ได้ทุกเมื่อเลย

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

l1.m: เรื่องน่าผิดหวัง
l1.hook: ทริปถูกยกเลิกแล้ว น่าเสียใจจริงๆ "bummer"
l1.ex: ทริปถูกยกเลิก? "What a bummer"

facts.mean: Scroll bad news for too long.
facts.def: To keep reading sad online news without stopping.

example.text: Stop doomscrolling and go to sleep.

misuse.text: Don't say 'doomscroll' about reading a recipe.

l1.m: เสพข่าวร้ายต่อเนื่อง
l1.hook: เที่ยงคืนแล้ว ยัง "doomscroll" ข่าวร้ายอยู่!
l1.ex: หยุด "doomscroll" แล้วไปนอนเถอะ

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

l1.hook: ดึกแล้ว ฉันง่วงมาก อยาก "catch some Zs"
l1.ex: ฉันจะ "catch some Zs"

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

l1.m: หายเป็นปกติ
l1.hook: นอนพักสั้นหนึ่งครั้ง แล้วฉันรู้สึก "good as new"
l1.ex: หลังจากนอนพัก ฉันรู้สึก "good as new"

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

l1.m: เริ่มต้นกัน
l1.hook: การประชุมเริ่มแล้ว ใครจะเริ่ม "get the ball rolling" ก่อน?
l1.ex: มาลอง "get the ball rolling" ด้วยไอเดียกันเถอะ

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

l1.hook: ฉันสามารถพึ่งพาเธอได้ไหม?
l1.ex: พิซซ่าเย็นนี้? "for sure"!

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

l1.hook: งานเลี้ยงจบตอนแปดโมงแล้ว จริงเหรอ?
l1.ex: งานปาร์ตี้นั้น "lame" ครับ.

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

l1.m: เพื่อนคู่แข่ง
l1.hook: เรายิ้มกัน แต่ก็แข่งขันกัน!
l1.ex: เธอเป็น "frenemy" ของฉัน, มักจะแข่งขันกับฉันเสมอ.

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

l1.hook: เสื้อโค้ทนั้นดูเหมือนภาพยนตร์เก่า!
l1.ex: เสื้อโค้ทนั้น "it's giving" สไตล์ดาราภาพยนตร์เก่า.

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

l1.hook: วันแย่ๆ แต่พรุ่งนี้กำลังมาถึง!
l1.ex: "chin up", พรุ่งนี้จะดีขึ้น.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

l1.hook: อาหารเย็นพร้อมแล้ว ใครหิวบ้าง? "dig in"
l1.ex: อาหารเย็นพร้อมแล้ว, เริ่ม "dig in" กันเลย!

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

l1.m: เจอกันใหม่นะ
l1.hook: ต้องไปแล้ว เริ่มเรียนแล้ว! "catch you later"
l1.ex: "catch you later" นะ, ฉันต้องไปแล้ว!

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

l1.m: ชัยชนะอย่างยิ่งใหญ่
l1.hook: ทำประตูในวินาทีสุดท้าย เราชนะ! "epic win"
l1.ex: เราทำประตูในวินาทีสุดท้าย "Epic win"!

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

l1.m: บอกตามตรงเลยนะ
l1.hook: พูดตรงๆ เกี่ยวกับหนังเรื่องนั้น? "ngl"
l1.ex: "Ngl", ฉันชอบหนังเรื่องนั้นมาก!

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

l1.hook: เค้กของฉันพังลง ทุกคนดู! "epic fail"
l1.ex: เค้กของฉันแบนลง, "epic fail" อย่างเต็มที่!

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

l1.hook: สอบพรุ่งนี้ เราจะเริ่มจากตรงไหน? "game plan"
l1.ex: แล้วเรามี game plan อย่างไร?

facts.def: People who love the same show or band.

example.text: The fandom loves this band.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers a 'fandom'.
misuse.why: It means devoted fans of one thing.

l1.m: กลุ่มแฟนคลับ
l1.hook: ใครใน "fandom" รักวงนี้ที่สุด?
l1.ex: "fandom" รักวงนี้

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

l1.m: เหนื่อยโฮก
l1.hook: การเดินป่านั้นทำให้ฉันรู้สึก "dog tired" เลย
l1.ex: ฉันรู้สึก "dog tired" หลังจากการเดินป้ายาวนั้น

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

l1.hook: ดูข้างนอก! เตรียมร่มไว้ เพราะกำลัง "raining cats and dogs"
l1.ex: มันกำลัง "raining cats and dogs"!

facts.def: Used to say you agree to a plan or want to do it.

example.text: We're going bowling tonight. Are you down?

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm down' when you feel sad.
misuse.why: It can also mean feeling low.

l1.hook: คืนนี้จะไปโบว์ลิ่ง ใครจะมาบ้าง? ถ้าคุณ "I'm down" บอกเลย
l1.ex: คืนนี้เราจะไปโบว์ลิ่ง คุณ "I'm down" หรือเปล่า?

facts.def: Used when something doesn't seem logical.

example.text: This game rule makes no sense.

misuse.text: Don't say 'makes no sense' about your boss's plan.

l1.m: ไม่มีเหตุผล
l1.hook: กฎเปลี่ยนอีกแล้ว ทำไม? มัน "makes no sense"
l1.ex: กฎเกมนี้ "makes no sense".

facts.def: Something unfair said to hurt someone.

example.text: That joke was a low blow.

misuse.text: Don't call fair criticism a 'low blow'.
misuse.why: It may just be honest feedback.

l1.m: คำพูดที่เจ็บแสบ
l1.hook: เขากล่าวถึงความผิดพลาดเก่าของเธอ! นั่นเป็น "low blow"
l1.ex: มุขตลกนั้นเป็น "low blow".

facts.mean: Grumpy and in a bad mood.
facts.def: Describes someone tired or annoyed.

example.text: I'm cranky before breakfast.

misuse.text: Don't call your boss 'cranky' in an email.

l1.m: อารมณ์เสีย
l1.hook: อย่าพูดกับฉันตอนนี้! ฉันกำลัง "cranky"
l1.ex: ฉัน "cranky" ก่อนอาหารเช้า.

facts.mean: A person who loves good food.
facts.def: Someone who enjoys trying and talking about food.
facts.hook: She reviews every restaurant in town!

example.text: My sister is a total foodie.

misuse.text: Don't call a chef a 'foodie'.
misuse.why: A chef cooks; a foodie loves eating.

l1.m: คนรักอาหาร
l1.hook: เธอรีวิวทุกร้านอาหารในเมือง! เธอเป็น "foodie"
l1.ex: พี่สาวของฉันเป็น "foodie" อย่างเต็มที่.

facts.def: Said politely after a match ends.

example.text: GG, that was a fun match!

misuse.text: Don't type 'GG' to your boss after a project.

l1.hook: เกมเพิ่งจบแล้ว, "GG"
l1.ex: "GG", สนุกมาก!

facts.def: A hand-on-face gesture of disbelief.

example.text: My phone was in my hand. Facepalm!

misuse.text: Don't 'facepalm' at your teacher's answer.

l1.m: การเอามือทบหน้าผาก (ด้วยความเอือมระอาหรือกุมขมับ)
l1.hook: เขาค้นหาโทรศัพท์ของเขา! ทำให้ฉัน "facepalm"
l1.ex: โทรศัพท์ของฉันอยู่ในมือของฉันเอง. "facepalm!"

facts.def: A day with extremely hot weather.

example.text: Today is a real scorcher!

misuse.text: Don't say 'scorcher' about a cold morning.
misuse.why: It means a very hot day.

l1.m: วันร้อนจัด
l1.hook: แดดร้อนจัด เหมือน 'scorcher' เลย แม้ในร่มก็ร้อน!
l1.ex: วันนี้เป็นวัน "scorcher" จริงๆ!

facts.def: Being included and informed about what's going on.

example.text: Keep me in the loop about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'in the loop' about a roller coaster.
misuse.why: It means knowing the latest news.

l1.m: รับข้อมูลล่าสุด
l1.hook: ไม่มีใครบอกข่าวฉันเลย ฉันไม่ได้อยู่ใน 'in the loop' นะ!
l1.ex: ช่วยทำให้ฉัน "in the loop" เกี่ยวกับการเดินทางด้วยนะ

facts.def: A polite way to say no or that you're okay.

example.text: No thanks, I'm good.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm good' if you want more food.

l1.hook: อยากได้เค้กเพิ่มไหม? ฉันบอกว่า 'I'm good' แล้ว!
l1.ex: ไม่เป็นไร ฉัน "I'm good"

facts.def: Used to show you aren't impressed.

example.text: The movie? Meh.

misuse.text: Don't say 'meh' about a friend's cooking.

l1.hook: หนังเป็นยังไง? ฉันรู้สึกว่า 'meh' ค่ะ!
l1.ex: หนังล่ะ? "Meh"

facts.def: Used for someone who makes a big deal out of small things.

example.text: Counting every cookie is petty, don't you think?

misuse.text: Don't call a real complaint 'petty'.

l1.m: ช่างขี้เครียดเรื่องเล็ก
l1.hook: เขาต้องการคุกกี้ของเขากลับมาหรือ? นั่นมัน 'petty' มากเลย!
l1.ex: การนับคุกกี้ทุกอันเป็นเรื่อง "petty" ไม่ใช่หรือ?

facts.def: Used to say that you are being completely honest.
facts.hook: Best pizza in town. Believe me?

example.text: This pizza is the best in town, no cap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no cap' about a baseball hat.

l1.hook: Şehrin en iyi pizzası. İnan bana, "no cap".
l1.ex: Bu pizza şehirdeki en iyisi, "no cap".

facts.def: Used when someone is upset or bitter, often after losing.

example.text: He's salty because I won the card game.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'salty' for giving homework.

l1.hook: Kaybetti, sonra somurtmaya başladı, "salty".
l1.ex: O, kart oyununu kazandığım için "salty".

facts.def: Used when something is so funny that you can't stop laughing.
facts.hook: The cat jumped in the box!

example.text: The cat jumped in the box. I'm dead!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm dead' about a sad story.

l1.hook: Kedi kutuya atladı! "I'm dead".
l1.ex: Kedi kutuya atladı. "I'm dead"!

facts.def: To eat a very large amount of food happily.

example.text: We pigged out on pizza last night.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host she made you 'pig out'.

l1.hook: Bütün pizza bitti! "pig out".
l1.ex: Geçen gece pizza yedik, "pig out".

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan or to say okay.

example.text: Pizza at six? Bet.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'bet' to your principal's email.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for formal messages.

l1.hook: Saat altıda pizza, anlaşma? "bet".
l1.ex: Saat altıda pizza? "Bet".

facts.def: Describes things that are very ordinary and popular. It can sound a bit mean.

example.text: My weekend plan is basic: pizza and a movie.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's gift 'basic' to her.

l1.hook: Yine pizza ve film mi?
l1.ex: Hafta sonu planım "basic": pizza ve film.

facts.def: A long-lasting disagreement between people.

example.text: They have beef over a game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'we have beef' about a small mix-up.
misuse.why: It sounds like a serious feud.

l1.hook: İkisi konuşmayı bıraktı. Neden?
l1.ex: Onların bir oyun yüzünden "beef"i var.

facts.def: Used for things with a beautiful, matching look.

example.text: Your desk looks so aesthetic.

misuse.text: Don't call your messy room 'aesthetic' to Mom.
misuse.why: It only fits stylish, pretty things.

l1.hook: Odan Pinterest gibi görünüyor!
l1.ex: Masan çok "aesthetic" görünüyor.

facts.def: To lose your temper quickly.

example.text: He blew a fuse over the messy room.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blow a fuse' about mild annoyance.

l1.hook: Baba dağınık odayı gördü!
l1.ex: O, dağınık oda yüzünden "blow a fuse" yaptı.

facts.def: Slang for food that tastes amazing.

example.text: Mom's pasta is bussin tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bussin' about a cold, bland sandwich.

l1.hook: Annemin makarnası bu gece inanılmaz lezzetli!
l1.ex: Annemin makarnası bu gece "bussin".

facts.def: A friendly reply to thanks.
facts.hook: Thanks so much for the ride!

example.text: Thanks for the ride! Anytime.

misuse.text: Don't say 'anytime' if you hate helping.

l1.hook: Yolculuk için çok teşekkür ederim!
l1.ex: Yolculuk için teşekkürler! Anytime.

facts.def: Used when you leave your game or chat for a short while.

example.text: Brb, I'll be AFK for five minutes.

misuse.text: Don't say 'AFK' in a formal email.

l1.hook: Beş dakika, sonra geri döneceğim!
l1.ex: Beş dakika AFK olacağım, brb.

facts.def: Used when you don't know the answer.

example.text: Where's the key? Beats me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'beats me' to a client's question.

l1.hook: Anahtar nereye gitti?
l1.ex: Anahtar nerede? Beats me.

facts.def: Used when your progress is lost and you must restart.

example.text: Plan failed. Back to square one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back to square one' after small progress.
misuse.why: It means you lost all progress.

l1.hook: Plan başarısız oldu. Şimdi ne yapacağız?
l1.ex: Plan başarısız oldu. Back to square one.

facts.def: Used when something costs a huge amount of money.

example.text: This coat costs an arm and a leg.

misuse.text: Don't take 'an arm and a leg' literally at the store.

l1.hook: Bu kabanın fiyatına bak!
l1.ex: Bu palto 'arm and a leg' kadar pahalı.

facts.def: Used to add a new, related thought in a talk.

example.text: By the way, the party starts at seven.

misuse.text: Don't use 'by the way' for your main point.
misuse.why: It signals a minor, extra comment.

l1.hook: by the way, oh bir şey daha!
l1.ex: by the way, parti saat yedide başlıyor.

facts.def: Used to say that something is excellent or very enjoyable.

example.text: You got us free tickets? That's awesome!

misuse.text: Don't say 'awesome' about sad news.

l1.hook: Ücretsiz biletler aldın? "awesome"
l1.ex: Ücretsiz biletler aldın? Bu "awesome"!

facts.def: Used when something matches your feeling perfectly.

example.text: That sleepy cat is a big mood.

misuse.text: Don't say 'big mood' about someone's real tragedy.

l1.hook: Uykulu kedi. Tam da hislerim. "big mood"
l1.ex: O uykulu kedi tam bir "big mood".

facts.mean: Do really well on a test.
facts.def: To get a top result on a test or task.
facts.hook: Test day. How did you do?

example.text: I aced my history test today!

misuse.text: Don't say you 'aced' a test you failed.

l1.hook: Sınav günü. Nasıl geçti? "ace"
l1.ex: Bugün tarih sınavımı 'ace' ettim!

facts.def: To watch several episodes of a show one after another.

example.text: I'll binge-watch this show all weekend.

misuse.text: Don't 'binge-watch' the night before exams.

l1.hook: Yağmurlu hafta sonu. Tüm sezon. Hadi "binge-watch"!
l1.ex: Bu diziyi hafta sonu boyunca "binge-watch" edeceğim.

facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

l1.hook: Çok fazla iş var. Ben 'burned out' oldum!
l1.ex: Sınavlardan sonra tamamen 'burned out' oldum.

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

l1.hook: Geçen hafta hastaydım, bugün 'back on my feet' oldum!
l1.ex: Nihayet 'back on my feet' oldum.

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

l1.hook: Buna hemen ihtiyacım var, 'ASAP'!
l1.ex: Lütfen notları 'ASAP' gönder.

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

l1.hook: Bu akşam saat altıda film, 'cool' mu?
l1.ex: 'cool', saat altıda görüşürüz!

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

l1.hook: O, hiç öğle yemeği için ödeme yapmaz, 'cheap'!
l1.ex: O, öğle yemeği almak için çok 'cheap'.

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

l1.hook: O, hatamı herkese 'call out' etti!
l1.ex: Geç kaldığım için beni "call out" etti.

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

l1.hook: Mülakat günü. Takım elbise ve kravat! "dressed to impress".
